# Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Control (bedrock-agentcore-control) Threat Model

[Threat Summary](#threat-summary) · [Threats](#threats) · [Mitigations](#mitigations) · [Implementations](#implementations) · [Appendix](#appendix)

## Overview

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Control is the management interface for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, a platform for building, deploying, and operating AI agents. Administrators and developers use it to configure the resources that agents depend on, without managing underlying infrastructure.

148 threats and 117 mitigations across 31 resource types and 171 API operations. 24 of 38 mitigation goals are covered, implemented by 300 implementations.

Source service model: [bedrock-agentcore-control](https://github.com/aws/api-models-aws/blob/3d89dd029ebd13b775ab5d22e5075399f20b35e4/models/bedrock-agentcore-control/service/2023-06-05/bedrock-agentcore-control-2023-06-05.json)

## Threats

Each scoping statement below describes the exposure the threat's mapped mitigations address. It assumes those mitigations are not applied and makes no claim about your resources.

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.1

Untrusted IAM principal, operating from a governed VPC network, can use the governed VPC network to make Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Control service API calls.

**Impacts:** [Data Collection](../threat-impacts.md#data-collection), [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.2](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-control2)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1537](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1537/)

**Scoping** (for [Identity Perimeter - Untrusted principal access from a governed VPC network](../potential-threats.md#identity-perimeter---untrusted-principal-access-from-a-governed-vpc-network)): Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Control is reachable from your VPC through an interface VPC endpoint (powered by AWS PrivateLink). An IAM principal from outside your organization can use that network path to make Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Control API calls with its own credentials.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:AddDatasetExamples` | `$.source.inlineExamples.examples[*]` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:ListDatasetExamples` | `$.datasetId` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateAgentRuntime` | `$.agentRuntimeArtifact.containerConfiguration.containerUri`, `$.environmentVariables{key}` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.2

IAM principal, with IAM permissions on untrusted Amazon Bedrock AgentCore resources, can interact with those untrusted resources from a governed VPC network.

**Impacts:** [Data Collection](../threat-impacts.md#data-collection), [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.1](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-control1)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1537](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1537/)

**Scoping** (for [Resource Perimeter - Access to untrusted resource from a governed VPC network](../potential-threats.md#resource-perimeter---access-to-untrusted-resource-from-a-governed-vpc-network)): AgentCore Control API calls from your VPCs can target datasets, memories, and other Amazon Bedrock AgentCore resources in another account. Using credentials with permissions on such a resource, an IAM principal on your network can write data to a dataset and read it back, or delete a memory.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:AddDatasetExamples` | `$.datasetId`, `$.source.inlineExamples.examples[*]` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:ListDatasetExamples` | `$.datasetId` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.1

My IAM principal, with IAM permissions to configure my Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime, can configure my Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime to use an untrusted identity provider to fetch the authorization server metadata and public keys used to validate the bearer tokens that callers present when invoking the agent runtime.

**Impacts:** [Data Collection](../threat-impacts.md#data-collection), [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.8](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime8)

**Scoping** (for [Resource Configuration - Data movement through an untrusted configured target](../potential-threats.md#resource-configuration---data-movement-through-an-untrusted-configured-target)): An IAM principal that creates or modifies your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime can set its custom JWT authorizer to an identity provider outside your organization or outside AWS. AgentCore Identity then fetches that provider's public keys and accepts the bearer tokens the provider issues for invoking your agent runtime.

**Data perimeter:** `CreateAgentRuntime` allows you to specify an external JWT authorizer as the value for the `authorizerConfiguration` request parameter. Because the subsequent requests against the external JWT authorizer are not governed by IAM, they are not restricted with `aws:ResourceOrgID` implemented in a service control policy.

**Data perimeter:** `UpdateAgentRuntime` allows you to specify an external JWT authorizer as the value for the `authorizerConfiguration` request parameter. Because the subsequent requests against the external JWT authorizer are not governed by IAM, they are not restricted with `aws:ResourceOrgID` implemented in a service control policy.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateAgentRuntime` | `$.authorizerConfiguration.customJWTAuthorizer.discoveryUrl` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateAgentRuntime` | `$.authorizerConfiguration.customJWTAuthorizer.discoveryUrl` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.2

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime that is not attached to a VPC, can use the agent runtime to send and receive traffic outside the network controls a VPC would enforce.

**Impacts:** [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration), [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion), [Lateral Movement](../threat-impacts.md#lateral-movement)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.5](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime5)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1048](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1048/), [T1578.002](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1578/002/)

**Scoping** (for [Ungoverned network traffic from non-VPC resources](../potential-threats.md#ungoverned-network-traffic-from-non-vpc-resources)): Your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime does not run in your VPCs when `$.networkConfiguration.networkMode` is set to `PUBLIC`. An IAM principal with create permissions can then use it to send and receive traffic outside the network controls a VPC would enforce, reaching the public internet.

**Data perimeter:** `CreateAgentRuntime` allows you to associate an agent runtime with an Amazon VPC to run your code.

**Data perimeter:** `UpdateAgentRuntime` allows you to associate a runtime with an Amazon VPC to run your code.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntime` | `$.payload` |
| `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand` | `$.body.command` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateAgentRuntime` | `$.networkConfiguration.networkMode` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateAgentRuntime` | `$.networkConfiguration.networkMode`, `$.networkConfiguration.networkModeConfig.requireServiceS3Endpoint` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.3

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create or modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime, can configure the agent runtime without required tagging information.

**Impacts:** [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.11](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime11)

**Scoping** (for [Resource missing required tags](../potential-threats.md#resource-missing-required-tags)): An IAM principal with permissions to create or modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime can omit the required tags, or remove them through `UntagResource`. An agent runtime left without those tags still hosts your agent code and may fall outside ownership attribution, cost allocation, and compliance inventory.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateAgentRuntime` | `$.tags{key}` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UntagResource` | `$.tagKeys[*]` |
| `resource-groups-tagging-api:UntagResources` | `$.ResourceARNList[*]`, `$.TagKeys[*]` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.4

Threat actor, with knowledge of a flawed inbound agent runtime custom JWT authorizer configuration, can take advantage of the flawed inbound agent runtime custom JWT authorizer configuration to gain unauthorized access to the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime.

**Impacts:** [Initial Access](../threat-impacts.md#initial-access)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.10](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime10)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1190](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/)

**Scoping** (for [Flawed authentication model problem](../potential-threats.md#flawed-authentication-model-problem)): The inbound custom JWT authorizer configuration of your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime lets callers invoke it with tokens that your OpenID Connect provider issues and your claim rules accept. A defect in that configuration can let a threat actor gain unauthorized access to the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntime` | `$.Mcp-Session-Id`, `$.X-Amzn-Bedrock-AgentCore-Runtime-Session-Id`, `$.X-Amzn-Bedrock-AgentCore-Runtime-User-Id`, `$.payload`, `$.qualifier` |
| `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand` | `$.X-Amzn-Bedrock-AgentCore-Runtime-Session-Id`, `$.body.command` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.5

Threat actor, with a method for enumerating public Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtimes, or prior knowledge of an existing public Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime, can access an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime that has been configured to allow public access.

**Impacts:** [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration), [Initial Access](../threat-impacts.md#initial-access)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.7](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime7)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1190](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/)

**Scoping** (for [Unintended public resource access](../potential-threats.md#unintended-public-resource-access)): An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime can be configured to allow public access through resource-based policies on the agent runtime and its endpoint that grant invocation actions to all principals. A threat actor with knowledge of such an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime can then call `InvokeAgentRuntime` or `InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand` and may retrieve data that your agent can reach.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntime` | `$.accountId`, `$.payload`, `$.qualifier` |
| `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand` | `$.body.command` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.6

My IAM principal, with IAM permissions on an untrusted Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime, can interact with the untrusted agent runtime, including sending data to it or receiving data from it.

**Impacts:** [Data Collection](../threat-impacts.md#data-collection), [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.4](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime4)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1537](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1537/)

**Scoping** (for [Resource Perimeter - Data exfiltration to untrusted resource](../potential-threats.md#resource-perimeter---data-exfiltration-to-untrusted-resource)): An agent runtime in an account outside your organization can grant your principals access through resource-based policies on both the runtime and its endpoint. Your principals that also hold permissions to invoke that runtime can then call `InvokeAgentRuntime` or `InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand` with their own credentials. They can send your data in `$.payload` or `$.body.command` to agent code that the runtime's owner controls.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntime` | `$.accountId`, `$.payload`, `$.qualifier` |
| `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand` | `$.accountId`, `$.body.command` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.7

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime, can create the agent runtime with its elastic network interfaces in a single Availability Zone.

**Impacts:** [Endpoint Denial of Service](../threat-impacts.md#endpoint-denial-of-service)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.6](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime6)

**Scoping** (for [Service disruption from single availability zone dependency](../potential-threats.md#service-disruption-from-single-availability-zone-dependency)): An IAM principal with permissions to create an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime can specify, on the default microVM compute type, VPC subnets in `$.networkConfiguration.networkModeConfig.subnets[*]` that place the agent runtime's network interfaces and agents in a single Availability Zone. An impairment of that zone can then sever the agent runtime's only network path into your VPC and interrupt `InvokeAgentRuntime` requests from its callers.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateAgentRuntime` | `$.networkConfiguration.networkModeConfig.subnets[*]` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateAgentRuntime` | `$.networkConfiguration.networkModeConfig.subnets[*]` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.8

IAM principal, with IAM permissions on my Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime and access to an unexpected network, can interact with my agent runtime from an unexpected network.

**Impacts:** [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration), [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion), [Initial Access](../threat-impacts.md#initial-access)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.3](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime3)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1078.004](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/004/), [T1556.009](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1556/009/)

**Scoping** (for [Network Perimeter - Resource access from unexpected network](../potential-threats.md#network-perimeter---resource-access-from-unexpected-network)): An IAM principal can send requests to your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime through the AgentCore public endpoints or an interface VPC endpoint (powered by AWS PrivateLink). An IAM principal with permissions on your agent runtime can call `InvokeAgentRuntime`, `DeleteAgentRuntime`, or `PutResourcePolicy` from an unexpected network.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntime` | `$.payload` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:DeleteAgentRuntime` | *(any parameter)* |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:PutResourcePolicy` | `$.policy` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.9

Untrusted IAM principal, that has been granted access to my Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime through its resource-based policy, can use my agent runtime.

**Impacts:** [Data Collection](../threat-impacts.md#data-collection), [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration), [Initial Access](../threat-impacts.md#initial-access), [Malicious Code Execution](../threat-impacts.md#malicious-code-execution)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.9](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime9)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1059.009](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/009/), [T1119](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1119/), [T1199](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1199/), [T1648](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1648/)

**Scoping** (for [Identity Perimeter - Untrusted principal access to my resources](../potential-threats.md#identity-perimeter---untrusted-principal-access-to-my-resources)): The resource-based policy on your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime can grant invocation and session access to principals outside your organization. Such a principal can call `InvokeAgentRuntime` or `InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand` to instruct your agent or run shell commands with your IAM execution role's credentials. It receives the resulting output and can end any runtime session whose ID it supplies to `StopRuntimeSession`.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntime` | `$.payload` |
| `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand` | `$.body.command` |
| `bedrock-agentcore:StopRuntimeSession` | `$.X-Amzn-Bedrock-AgentCore-Runtime-Session-Id` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.10

Threat actor, with knowledge of a vulnerable OIDC identity provider that has been configured in the custom JWT authorizer of an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime, can gain federated access to the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime and the agent it hosts.

**Impacts:** [Initial Access](../threat-impacts.md#initial-access)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.10](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime10)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1190](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/)

**Scoping** (for [Vulnerable identity provider problem](../potential-threats.md#vulnerable-identity-provider-problem)): An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime delegates authentication for invocations of your agent to the OpenID Connect identity provider you configure in its inbound JWT authorizer. If that identity provider is vulnerable, a threat actor presenting a forged or improperly issued token can gain federated access to your agent.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntime` | `$.payload`, `$.qualifier` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.11

Untrusted IAM principal, that has been granted access to my Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime's IAM execution role through its trust policy, can assume my execution role and act with its permissions.

**Impacts:** [Data Collection](../threat-impacts.md#data-collection), [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration), [Initial Access](../threat-impacts.md#initial-access)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.2](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime2)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1048](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1048/), [T1078.004](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/004/), [T1530](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1530/)

**Scoping** (for [Identity Perimeter - Untrusted principal assumption of my IAM roles](../potential-threats.md#identity-perimeter---untrusted-principal-assumption-of-my-iam-roles)): Your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime designates an IAM execution role through `$.roleArn`, and you author its trust policy. That trust policy can allow identities outside your organization to assume the role and act with its permissions.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateAgentRuntime` | `$.roleArn` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateAgentRuntime` | `$.roleArn` |
| `sts:AssumeRole` | `$.RoleArn` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.12

Threat actor, with possession of credentials for my Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime's execution role, can use my execution role while on an unexpected network.

**Impacts:** [Credential Theft](../threat-impacts.md#credential-theft), [Data Collection](../threat-impacts.md#data-collection), [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.1](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime1)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1048](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1048/), [T1078.004](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/004/), [T1606](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1606/)

**Scoping** (for [Network Perimeter - Credential use from unexpected network](../potential-threats.md#network-perimeter---credential-use-from-unexpected-network)): Amazon Bedrock AgentCore delivers temporary credentials for your agent runtime's execution role to the agent or tool code that the runtime hosts. A threat actor who obtains those credentials can use that execution role while on an unexpected network.

**Data perimeter:** `CreateAgentRuntime` allows you to specify a service role, referred to as the AgentCore Runtime execution role, for your AgentCore Runtime operations. The service uses the role to make AWS API calls from your code.

**Data perimeter:** `UpdateAgentRuntime` allows you to specify a service role for your AgentCore Runtime operations. The service uses the role to make AWS API calls from your code.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore:GetWorkloadAccessTokenForUserId` | `$.userId`, `$.workloadName` |
| `bedrock-runtime:InvokeModel` | `$.body`, `$.modelId` |
| `cloudwatch-logs:PutLogEvents` | `$.logEvents[*].message`, `$.logGroupName`, `$.logStreamName` |
| `ecr:GetDownloadUrlForLayer` | `$.layerDigest`, `$.repositoryName` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.13

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to use an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime, can interact with the agent runtime without a record of their activities being persisted by vended application log delivery.

**Impacts:** [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.13](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime13)

**Scoping** (for [Defense evasion through unconfigured logging](../potential-threats.md#defense-evasion-through-unconfigured-logging)): When vended application log delivery is not configured on your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime, no vended application log records are written by vended application log delivery. An IAM principal with permissions to use the agent runtime can invoke it, leaving no record of those invocations persisted by vended application log delivery.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntime` | `$.X-Amzn-Bedrock-AgentCore-Runtime-Session-Id`, `$.payload`, `$.qualifier` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.14

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime's CloudWatch Logs vended log delivery, can disable application log delivery for the agent runtime.

**Impacts:** [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.13](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime13)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1562.008](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/008/)

**Scoping** (for [Logging disablement](../potential-threats.md#logging-disablement)): An IAM principal with permissions to modify your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime's CloudWatch Logs vended log delivery can call `DeleteDelivery`, then `DeleteDeliverySource`, to remove its log delivery. That change stops the agent runtime's opt-in application logs from reaching CloudWatch Logs while invocations continue.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `cloudwatch-logs:DeleteDelivery` | `$.id` |
| `cloudwatch-logs:DeleteDeliverySource` | `$.name` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.15

Threat actor, with control of an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime configured with overly permissive outbound security group rules, can use the agent runtime to interact with ungoverned network destinations.

**Impacts:** [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration), [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.12](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime12)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1048](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1048/)

**Protocols:** `HTTPS`, `HTTP`

**Scoping** (for [Data exfiltration through overly-permissive outbound security group rules](../potential-threats.md#data-exfiltration-through-overly-permissive-outbound-security-group-rules)): In VPC network mode, the security groups you specify attach to AgentCore-managed network interfaces in your subnets, where their outbound rules govern your agent runtime's connections. Where those rules permit an unrestricted destination range, a threat actor controlling the agent runtime can use it to interact with ungoverned network destinations.

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntimeEndpoint.1

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create or modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime endpoint, can configure the agent runtime endpoint without required tagging information.

**Impacts:** [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntimeEndpoint.5](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntimeendpoint5)

**Scoping** (for [Resource missing required tags](../potential-threats.md#resource-missing-required-tags)): An IAM principal with permissions to create or modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime endpoint can omit the required tags, or remove them later through `UntagResource`. An agent runtime endpoint left without those tags still routes agent invocations and may fall outside ownership attribution, cost allocation, and compliance inventory.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateAgentRuntimeEndpoint` | `$.tags{key}` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:TagResource` | `$.tags{key}` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UntagResource` | `$.tagKeys[*]` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntimeEndpoint.2

Threat actor, with a method for enumerating public Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime endpoints, or prior knowledge of an existing public Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime endpoint, can access an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime endpoint that has been configured to allow public access.

**Impacts:** [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration), [Initial Access](../threat-impacts.md#initial-access)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntimeEndpoint.3](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntimeendpoint3)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1190](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/)

**Scoping** (for [Unintended public resource access](../potential-threats.md#unintended-public-resource-access)): An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime endpoint can be configured to allow access from any AWS account through wildcard-principal grants in the resource-based policies of the endpoint and its parent agent runtime. A threat actor with knowledge of such an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime endpoint can then call `GetAgentCard`, `InvokeAgentRuntime`, or `InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand`, sending prompts or shell commands that may extract data the agent's IAM execution role can reach.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore:GetAgentCard` | `$.qualifier` |
| `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntime` | `$.payload`, `$.qualifier` |
| `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand` | `$.body.command`, `$.qualifier` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntimeEndpoint.3

My IAM principal, with IAM permissions on an untrusted Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime endpoint, can interact with the untrusted agent runtime endpoint, including sending data to it or receiving data from it.

**Impacts:** [Data Collection](../threat-impacts.md#data-collection), [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntimeEndpoint.2](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntimeendpoint2)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1537](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1537/)

**Scoping** (for [Resource Perimeter - Data exfiltration to untrusted resource](../potential-threats.md#resource-perimeter---data-exfiltration-to-untrusted-resource)): An agent runtime endpoint in an account outside your organization can grant your principals access through resource-based policies on the endpoint and its runtime. Your principals can then call `InvokeAgentRuntime` or `InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand` with that endpoint's name in `$.qualifier` and send your data in `$.payload` or `$.body.command`. The endpoint owner's agent code, logs, and storage can retain that data outside your governance.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntime` | `$.accountId`, `$.payload`, `$.qualifier` |
| `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand` | `$.accountId`, `$.body.command`, `$.qualifier` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntimeEndpoint.4

IAM principal, with IAM permissions on my Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime endpoint and access to an unexpected network, can interact with my agent runtime endpoint from an unexpected network.

**Impacts:** [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration), [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion), [Initial Access](../threat-impacts.md#initial-access)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntimeEndpoint.1](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntimeendpoint1)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1048](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1048/), [T1078.004](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/004/), [T1556.009](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1556/009/)

**Scoping** (for [Network Perimeter - Resource access from unexpected network](../potential-threats.md#network-perimeter---resource-access-from-unexpected-network)): An IAM principal can send requests to your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime endpoint through the public AgentCore endpoints or an interface VPC endpoint (powered by AWS PrivateLink). An IAM principal with permissions on your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime endpoint can call `InvokeAgentRuntime`, `UpdateAgentRuntimeEndpoint`, or `PutResourcePolicy` against it from an unexpected network.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntime` | `$.payload`, `$.qualifier` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:PutResourcePolicy` | `$.policy` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateAgentRuntimeEndpoint` | `$.agentRuntimeVersion` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntimeEndpoint.5

Untrusted IAM principal, that has been granted access to my Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime endpoint through its resource-based policy, can use my Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime endpoint.

**Impacts:** [Data Collection](../threat-impacts.md#data-collection), [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration), [Initial Access](../threat-impacts.md#initial-access), [Malicious Code Execution](../threat-impacts.md#malicious-code-execution)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntimeEndpoint.4](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntimeendpoint4)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1048](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1048/), [T1119](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1119/), [T1199](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1199/), [T1648](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1648/)

**Scoping** (for [Identity Perimeter - Untrusted principal access to my resources](../potential-threats.md#identity-perimeter---untrusted-principal-access-to-my-resources)): A resource-based policy on your agent runtime endpoint can grant invocation access to principals outside your organization. If your agent runtime's resource-based policy also grants access, such a principal can call `InvokeAgentRuntime` or `InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand` through this endpoint with its own credentials. It can send prompts that make your agent act with its IAM execution role, or run shell commands inside the agent's microVM.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntime` | `$.payload`, `$.qualifier` |
| `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand` | `$.X-Amzn-Bedrock-AgentCore-Runtime-Session-Id`, `$.body.command`, `$.qualifier` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.ApiKeyCredentialProvider.1

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create or modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore API key credential provider, can configure the API key credential provider without required tagging information.

**Impacts:** [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.ApiKeyCredentialProvider.1](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlapikeycredentialprovider1)

**Scoping** (for [Resource missing required tags](../potential-threats.md#resource-missing-required-tags)): An IAM principal with permissions to create or modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore API key credential provider can omit the required tags, leaving `$.tags{key}` unset or removing them through `UntagResource`. An API key credential provider left without those tags still supplies its third-party API key and may fall outside ownership attribution, cost allocation, and compliance inventory.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateApiKeyCredentialProvider` | `$.tags{key}` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UntagResource` | `$.tagKeys[*]` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.ApiKeyCredentialProvider.2

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to use an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore API key credential provider, can interact with the API key credential provider without a record of their activities being persisted by AgentCore Identity tracing.

**Impacts:** [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.ApiKeyCredentialProvider.2](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlapikeycredentialprovider2)

**Scoping** (for [Defense evasion through unconfigured logging](../potential-threats.md#defense-evasion-through-unconfigured-logging)): When AgentCore Identity tracing is not configured on your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore API key credential provider, no trace spans are written by AgentCore Identity tracing. An IAM principal with permissions to use the API key credential provider can interact with it, leaving no record of those interactions persisted by AgentCore Identity tracing.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore:GetResourceApiKey` | `$.workloadIdentityToken` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.ApiKeyCredentialProvider.3

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore API key credential provider, can disable TRACES vended log delivery for the API key credential provider.

**Impacts:** [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.ApiKeyCredentialProvider.2](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlapikeycredentialprovider2)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1562.008](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/008/)

**Scoping** (for [Logging disablement](../potential-threats.md#logging-disablement)): An IAM principal with permissions to modify your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore API key credential provider can use CloudWatch Logs permissions to call `DeleteDelivery` on its deliveries, then `DeleteDeliverySource`. Deleting them stops the provider's opt-in trace spans from reaching AWS X-Ray or CloudWatch Logs while later `GetResourceApiKey` calls continue without these records; a `DeleteDelivery` call with a single delivery ID in `$.id` stops only that delivery's records.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `cloudwatch-logs:DeleteDelivery` | `$.id` |
| `cloudwatch-logs:DeleteDeliverySource` | `$.name` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Browser.1

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to invoke an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore browser that is not attached to a VPC, can use the browser to send and receive traffic outside the network controls a VPC would enforce.

**Impacts:** [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration), [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion), [Lateral Movement](../threat-impacts.md#lateral-movement)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Browser.3](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlbrowser3)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1048](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1048/)

**Scoping** (for [Ungoverned network traffic from non-VPC resources](../potential-threats.md#ungoverned-network-traffic-from-non-vpc-resources)): Your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore browser does not run in your VPCs when `$.networkConfiguration.networkMode` is `PUBLIC` or `$.browserIdentifier` names the `aws.browser.v1` system browser. An IAM principal with invoke permissions can then use it to send and receive traffic outside the network controls a VPC would enforce, reaching internet endpoints, including the proxy servers in `$.proxyConfiguration.proxies[*].externalProxy.server`.

**Data perimeter:** `CreateBrowser` allows you to associate a custom browser with an Amazon VPC to run your code.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeBrowser` | `$.action.keyType.text` |
| `bedrock-agentcore:StartBrowserSession` | `$.browserIdentifier`, `$.proxyConfiguration.proxies[*].externalProxy.server` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateBrowser` | `$.networkConfiguration.networkMode` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Browser.2

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create or modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore browser, can configure the browser without required tagging information.

**Impacts:** [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Browser.5](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlbrowser5)

**Scoping** (for [Resource missing required tags](../potential-threats.md#resource-missing-required-tags)): An IAM principal with permissions to create or modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore browser can omit the required tags, or remove them later through `UntagResource`. A browser left without those tags still runs sessions for your agents and may fall outside ownership attribution, cost allocation, and compliance inventory.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateBrowser` | `$.tags{key}` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UntagResource` | `$.tagKeys[*]` |
| `resource-groups-tagging-api:UntagResources` | `$.ResourceARNList[*]`, `$.TagKeys[*]` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Browser.3

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore browser, can create the browser with its elastic network interfaces in a single Availability Zone.

**Impacts:** [Endpoint Denial of Service](../threat-impacts.md#endpoint-denial-of-service)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Browser.4](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlbrowser4)

**Scoping** (for [Service disruption from single availability zone dependency](../potential-threats.md#service-disruption-from-single-availability-zone-dependency)): An IAM principal with permissions to create an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore browser can use `$.networkConfiguration.vpcConfig.subnets[*]` to place the browser's network interfaces in a single Availability Zone. An impairment of that zone can then sever those network interfaces and leave your agents' browser sessions unable to load web pages or reach private resources.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateBrowser` | `$.networkConfiguration.networkMode`, `$.networkConfiguration.vpcConfig.subnets[*]` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Browser.4

Untrusted IAM principal, that has been granted access to my Amazon Bedrock AgentCore browser's IAM execution role through its trust policy, can assume my execution role and act with its permissions.

**Impacts:** [Data Collection](../threat-impacts.md#data-collection), [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration), [Initial Access](../threat-impacts.md#initial-access)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Browser.2](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlbrowser2)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1048](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1048/), [T1078.004](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/004/), [T1530](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1530/)

**Scoping** (for [Identity Perimeter - Untrusted principal assumption of my IAM roles](../potential-threats.md#identity-perimeter---untrusted-principal-assumption-of-my-iam-roles)): Your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore browser designates an optional IAM execution role through `$.executionRoleArn`, and you author its trust policy. That trust policy can allow identities outside your organization to assume the role and act with its permissions.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateBrowser` | `$.executionRoleArn` |
| `sts:AssumeRole` | `$.RoleArn` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Browser.5

Threat actor, with possession of credentials for my Amazon Bedrock AgentCore browser's execution role, can use my execution role while on an unexpected network.

**Impacts:** [Data Collection](../threat-impacts.md#data-collection), [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Browser.1](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlbrowser1)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1048](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1048/), [T1530](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1530/)

**Scoping** (for [Network Perimeter - Credential use from unexpected network](../potential-threats.md#network-perimeter---credential-use-from-unexpected-network)): When you specify your browser's execution role in `CreateBrowser`, each session's microVM receives temporary credentials for that role from the MicroVM Metadata Service (MMDS). A threat actor who obtains those credentials can use that execution role while on an unexpected network.

**Data perimeter:** `CreateBrowser` allows you to specify a service role for your AgentCore Browser operations. The service uses the role to make AWS API calls from your code.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `cloudwatch-logs:PutLogEvents` | `$.logEvents[*].message`, `$.logGroupName`, `$.logStreamName` |
| `s3:GetObject` | `$.Bucket`, `$.Key` |
| `s3:PutObject` | `$.Body`, `$.Bucket`, `$.Key` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Browser.6

Threat actor, with control of an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore browser configured with overly permissive outbound security group rules, can use the browser to interact with ungoverned network destinations.

**Impacts:** [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration), [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Browser.6](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlbrowser6)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1048](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1048/)

**Protocols:** `HTTPS`, `HTTP`

**Scoping** (for [Data exfiltration through overly-permissive outbound security group rules](../potential-threats.md#data-exfiltration-through-overly-permissive-outbound-security-group-rules)): In VPC network mode, the outbound rules of the security groups you specify at creation govern the browser's connections from network interfaces in your subnets. Where those rules permit an unrestricted destination range, a threat actor controlling the browser can use it to interact with ungoverned network destinations.

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.BrowserProfile.1

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create or modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore browser profile, can configure the browser profile without required tagging information.

**Impacts:** [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.BrowserProfile.1](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlbrowserprofile1)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1562](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/)

**Scoping** (for [Resource missing required tags](../potential-threats.md#resource-missing-required-tags)): An IAM principal with permissions to create or modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore browser profile can omit the required tags, or remove them through `UntagResource`. A browser profile left without those tags still stores cookies for later sessions and may fall outside ownership attribution, cost allocation, and compliance inventory.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateBrowserProfile` | `$.tags{key}` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UntagResource` | `$.tagKeys[*]` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CapacityProvider.1

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore capacity provider, can encrypt the agent session data stored on its root volume, ephemeral EBS volume, and persistent volume with key material outside the AWS account owner's control.

**Impacts:** [Data Encrypted for Impact](../threat-impacts.md#data-encrypted-for-impact), [Inhibit System Recovery](../threat-impacts.md#inhibit-system-recovery)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CapacityProvider.6](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlcapacityprovider6)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1486](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1486/)

**Scoping** (for [Data loss through inaccessible encryption key](../potential-threats.md#data-loss-through-inaccessible-encryption-key)): An IAM principal able to create your capacity provider chooses the KMS key that encrypts the agent session data on its EBS volumes by setting `$.computeConfiguration.ec2Configuration.rootVolume.kmsKeyId` and `$.computeConfiguration.ec2Configuration.launchTemplateSource.launchParameters.ephemeralVolumes[*].ebs.kmsKeyId` and `$.computeConfiguration.ec2Configuration.volumes[*].ebsConfiguration.kmsKeyId`. If that key material sits outside your control, its holder can later revoke or delete it and leave that session data unreadable.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateCapacityProvider` | `$.computeConfiguration.ec2Configuration.launchTemplateSource.launchParameters.ephemeralVolumes[*].ebs.kmsKeyId`, `$.computeConfiguration.ec2Configuration.rootVolume.kmsKeyId`, `$.computeConfiguration.ec2Configuration.volumes[*].ebsConfiguration.kmsKeyId` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CapacityProvider.2

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create or modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore capacity provider, can configure the capacity provider without required tagging information.

**Impacts:** [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CapacityProvider.8](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlcapacityprovider8)

**Scoping** (for [Resource missing required tags](../potential-threats.md#resource-missing-required-tags)): An IAM principal with permissions to create or modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore capacity provider can omit the required tags, or remove them through `UntagResource`. A capacity provider left without those tags still launches Amazon EC2 managed instances and may fall outside ownership attribution, cost allocation, and compliance inventory.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateCapacityProvider` | `$.tags{key}` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UntagResource` | `$.tagKeys[*]` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CapacityProvider.3

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore capacity provider, can encrypt the capacity provider's root volume, ephemeral EBS volume, and persistent volume with an AWS managed KMS key, limiting your ability to govern the key's policy and lifecycle.

**Impacts:** [Data Collection](../threat-impacts.md#data-collection), [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CapacityProvider.6](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlcapacityprovider6)

**Scoping** (for [Limited encryption governance with AWS owned or managed KMS keys](../potential-threats.md#limited-encryption-governance-with-aws-owned-or-managed-kms-keys)): An IAM principal able to create your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore capacity provider chooses whether the AWS managed key protects its root volume, ephemeral EBS volume, and persistent volume at rest. You cannot govern that key's policy or lifecycle.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateCapacityProvider` | `$.computeConfiguration.ec2Configuration.launchTemplateSource.launchParameters.ephemeralVolumes[*].ebs.kmsKeyId`, `$.computeConfiguration.ec2Configuration.rootVolume.kmsKeyId`, `$.computeConfiguration.ec2Configuration.volumes[*].ebsConfiguration.kmsKeyId` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CapacityProvider.4

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create or modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore capacity provider that supports detailed monitoring for the Amazon EC2 managed instances it launches, can create or configure the capacity provider without detailed monitoring enabled.

**Impacts:** [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CapacityProvider.9](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlcapacityprovider9)

**Scoping** (for [Defense evasion through unconfigured enhanced monitoring](../potential-threats.md#defense-evasion-through-unconfigured-enhanced-monitoring)): An IAM principal can create an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore capacity provider whose Amazon EC2 managed instances run without detailed monitoring. Without 1-minute CPU and network metrics from those instances, anomalous activity, such as a cryptomining burst or data exfiltration, blends into 5-minute aggregates.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateCapacityProvider` | `$.computeConfiguration.ec2Configuration.launchTemplateSource.launchParameters.monitoring` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CapacityProvider.5

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore capacity provider, can configure the capacity provider on creation to not use encryption at rest.

**Impacts:** [Data Collection](../threat-impacts.md#data-collection), [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CapacityProvider.3](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlcapacityprovider3), [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CapacityProvider.6](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlcapacityprovider6)

**Scoping** (for [Data exposure from missing encryption at rest](../potential-threats.md#data-exposure-from-missing-encryption-at-rest)): Encryption at rest is an optional setting on your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore capacity provider, chosen when you create it. An IAM principal with permissions to create the capacity provider can leave the agent data on its Amazon EBS volumes without encryption at rest.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateCapacityProvider` | `$.computeConfiguration.ec2Configuration.launchTemplateSource.launchParameters.ephemeralVolumes[*].ebs.encrypted`, `$.computeConfiguration.ec2Configuration.rootVolume.encrypted`, `$.computeConfiguration.ec2Configuration.volumes[*].ebsConfiguration.encrypted` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CapacityProvider.6

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore capacity provider, can create the capacity provider with its Amazon EC2 managed instances and network interfaces in a single Availability Zone.

**Impacts:** [Endpoint Denial of Service](../threat-impacts.md#endpoint-denial-of-service)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CapacityProvider.7](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlcapacityprovider7)

**Scoping** (for [Service disruption from single availability zone dependency](../potential-threats.md#service-disruption-from-single-availability-zone-dependency)): An IAM principal with permissions to create an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore capacity provider can set `$.computeConfiguration.ec2Configuration.vpcConfiguration.subnets[*]` to place its Amazon EC2 managed instances and network interfaces in a single Availability Zone. An impairment of that zone can then leave every agent runtime associated with the capacity provider without reachable instances for its sessions and invocations.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateCapacityProvider` | `$.computeConfiguration.ec2Configuration.vpcConfiguration.subnets[*]` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CapacityProvider.7

Threat actor, who controls a VPC-connected resource in the same VPC as an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore capacity provider, can interact with the capacity provider's Amazon EC2 managed instances through overly permissive network rules and move laterally within the VPC.

**Impacts:** [Lateral Movement](../threat-impacts.md#lateral-movement)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CapacityProvider.10](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlcapacityprovider10)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1021](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/)

**Protocols:** `HTTP`, `SSH`

**Scoping** (for [Lateral movement through permissive network rules](../potential-threats.md#lateral-movement-through-permissive-network-rules)): Each session on your capacity provider runs your agents on an Amazon EC2 managed instance with a network interface in your VPC subnets. A threat actor controlling another resource in that VPC can reach those network interfaces through overly permissive network rules and move laterally.

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CapacityProvider.8

Threat actor, with network access to an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore capacity provider that permits traffic to services and administrative ports from unrestricted sources, can reach listening services and administrative ports on the capacity provider.

**Impacts:** [Account and Resource Discovery](../threat-impacts.md#account-and-resource-discovery), [Initial Access](../threat-impacts.md#initial-access)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CapacityProvider.10](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlcapacityprovider10)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1046](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1046/), [T1190](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/)

**Protocols:** `SSH`, `HTTP`

**Scoping** (for [Network exposure through overly-permissive inbound security group rules](../potential-threats.md#network-exposure-through-overly-permissive-inbound-security-group-rules)): AgentCore associates the security groups you specify on a capacity provider with the Amazon EC2 managed instances that run your agents in your VPC. An inbound rule permitting an unrestricted source range lets any host that can route to those instances reach their listening services and administrative ports.

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CapacityProvider.9

Threat actor, with network access to an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore capacity provider that has been placed in a public subnet, can access the capacity provider directly from an ungoverned network.

**Impacts:** [Account and Resource Discovery](../threat-impacts.md#account-and-resource-discovery), [Initial Access](../threat-impacts.md#initial-access)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CapacityProvider.4](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlcapacityprovider4)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1190](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/)

**Protocols:** `SSH`, `HTTP`

**Scoping** (for [Public subnet resource exposure](../potential-threats.md#public-subnet-resource-exposure)): An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore capacity provider launches its Amazon EC2 managed instances and their network interfaces in the subnets you choose for it. A capacity provider placed in a subnet that routes to an internet gateway can be reached directly from an ungoverned network when those instances have a public IP address.

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CapacityProvider.10

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create or update an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore capacity provider, can configure the capacity provider to use an instance type that does not provide automatic encryption of instance-to-instance traffic.

**Impacts:** [Data Collection](../threat-impacts.md#data-collection)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CapacityProvider.5](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlcapacityprovider5)

**Scoping** (for [Unencrypted instance-to-instance traffic through instance type selection](../potential-threats.md#unencrypted-instance-to-instance-traffic-through-instance-type-selection)): An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore capacity provider's allowed instance types setting, `$.computeConfiguration.ec2Configuration.launchTemplateSource.launchParameters.instanceRequirements.allowedInstanceTypes[*]`, accepts Amazon EC2 instance types that do not provide automatic encryption of instance-to-instance traffic. If such a type is selected, traffic between the capacity provider's instances and other instances you operate is carried without that encryption.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateCapacityProvider` | `$.computeConfiguration.ec2Configuration.launchTemplateSource.launchParameters.instanceRequirements.allowedInstanceTypes[*]` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CapacityProvider.11

Untrusted IAM principal, that has been granted access to my Amazon Bedrock AgentCore capacity provider's IAM infrastructure role and instance role through their trust policies, can assume my infrastructure role and instance role and act with their permissions.

**Impacts:** [Account and Resource Discovery](../threat-impacts.md#account-and-resource-discovery), [Initial Access](../threat-impacts.md#initial-access), [Resource Hijacking](../threat-impacts.md#resource-hijacking)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CapacityProvider.2](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlcapacityprovider2)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1078.004](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/004/), [T1496.001](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1496/001/), [T1580](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1580/)

**Scoping** (for [Identity Perimeter - Untrusted principal assumption of my IAM roles](../potential-threats.md#identity-perimeter---untrusted-principal-assumption-of-my-iam-roles)): Your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore capacity provider designates an infrastructure role and an instance role in a custom or default instance profile through `$.permissionsConfiguration.capacityProviderOperatorRoleArn`, `$.computeConfiguration.ec2Configuration.launchTemplateSource.launchParameters.instanceProfileArn`, and you author their trust policies. Those trust policies can allow identities outside your organization to assume the roles and act with their permissions, such as launching Amazon EC2 instances.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateCapacityProvider` | `$.computeConfiguration.ec2Configuration.launchTemplateSource.launchParameters.instanceProfileArn`, `$.permissionsConfiguration.capacityProviderOperatorRoleArn` |
| `sts:AssumeRole` | `$.RoleArn` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CapacityProvider.12

Threat actor, with possession of credentials for my Amazon Bedrock AgentCore capacity provider's instance profile or default instance role, can use my instance profile or default instance role while on an unexpected network.

**Impacts:** [Data Collection](../threat-impacts.md#data-collection), [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CapacityProvider.1](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlcapacityprovider1)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1078.004](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/004/)

**Scoping** (for [Network Perimeter - Credential use from unexpected network](../potential-threats.md#network-perimeter---credential-use-from-unexpected-network)): Amazon EC2 delivers temporary credentials for your capacity provider's instance profile or default instance role through instance metadata to each managed instance the capacity provider launches. A threat actor who obtains those credentials can use either role while on an unexpected network.

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CapacityProvider.13

Threat actor, with control of an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore capacity provider configured with overly permissive outbound security group rules, can use the capacity provider to interact with ungoverned network destinations.

**Impacts:** [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration), [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CapacityProvider.10](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlcapacityprovider10)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1048](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1048/)

**Protocols:** `HTTPS`, `HTTP`, `DNS`, `SSH`

**Scoping** (for [Data exfiltration through overly-permissive outbound security group rules](../potential-threats.md#data-exfiltration-through-overly-permissive-outbound-security-group-rules)): The outbound rules of the security groups you specify when creating the capacity provider govern connections from every Amazon EC2 managed instance it launches. Where those rules permit an unrestricted destination range, a threat actor controlling the capacity provider can use it to interact with ungoverned network destinations.

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CapacityProvider.14

Threat actor, who can execute code in an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore capacity provider that is attached to a subnet with a route to an internet gateway, can send the capacity provider's outbound traffic directly to the public internet instead of through a governed network egress path.

**Impacts:** [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration), [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CapacityProvider.4](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlcapacityprovider4)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1048](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1048/)

**Protocols:** `HTTPS`, `HTTP`, `DNS`

**Scoping** (for [Uncontrolled internet egress through public-subnet routing](../potential-threats.md#uncontrolled-internet-egress-through-public-subnet-routing)): Your capacity provider's VPC configuration places the Amazon EC2 managed instances that run your agents, with the network interfaces that carry their outbound traffic, in the subnets you specify. Where those subnets route to an internet gateway, code running on those instances can reach the public internet directly when those interfaces have a public IP address.

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CodeInterpreter.1

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to invoke an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore code interpreter that is not attached to a VPC, can use the code interpreter to send and receive traffic outside the network controls a VPC would enforce.

**Impacts:** [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration), [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion), [Lateral Movement](../threat-impacts.md#lateral-movement)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CodeInterpreter.3](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlcodeinterpreter3)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1048](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1048/), [T1578.002](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1578/002/)

**Scoping** (for [Ungoverned network traffic from non-VPC resources](../potential-threats.md#ungoverned-network-traffic-from-non-vpc-resources)): Your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore code interpreter does not run in your VPCs when its network mode (`$.networkConfiguration.networkMode`) is `PUBLIC` or `SANDBOX`. An IAM principal with invoke permissions can then use it to send and receive traffic outside the network controls a VPC would enforce, reaching the public internet in `PUBLIC` mode or Amazon S3 in `SANDBOX` mode.

**Data perimeter:** `CreateCodeInterpreter` allows you to associate a custom code interpreter with an Amazon VPC to run your code.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeCodeInterpreter` | `$.arguments.code`, `$.arguments.command` |
| `bedrock-agentcore:StartCodeInterpreterSession` | *(any parameter)* |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateCodeInterpreter` | `$.networkConfiguration.networkMode` |
| `s3:PutObject` | `$.Bucket` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CodeInterpreter.2

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create or modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore code interpreter, can configure the code interpreter without required tagging information.

**Impacts:** [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CodeInterpreter.5](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlcodeinterpreter5)

**Scoping** (for [Resource missing required tags](../potential-threats.md#resource-missing-required-tags)): An IAM principal with permissions to create or modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore code interpreter can omit the required tags, or remove them through `UntagResource`. A code interpreter left without those tags still runs code in its sessions and may fall outside ownership attribution, cost allocation, and compliance inventory.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateCodeInterpreter` | `$.tags{key}` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UntagResource` | `$.tagKeys[*]` |
| `resource-groups-tagging-api:UntagResources` | `$.ResourceARNList[*]`, `$.TagKeys[*]` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CodeInterpreter.3

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore code interpreter, can create the code interpreter with its elastic network interfaces in a single Availability Zone.

**Impacts:** [Endpoint Denial of Service](../threat-impacts.md#endpoint-denial-of-service)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CodeInterpreter.4](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlcodeinterpreter4)

**Scoping** (for [Service disruption from single availability zone dependency](../potential-threats.md#service-disruption-from-single-availability-zone-dependency)): An IAM principal with permissions to create an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore code interpreter can set `$.networkConfiguration.vpcConfig.subnets[*]` to subnets that place the code interpreter's elastic network interfaces and sessions in a single Availability Zone. An impairment of that zone can then make those network interfaces unreachable and leave your agents unable to start or invoke code interpreter sessions.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateCodeInterpreter` | `$.networkConfiguration.vpcConfig.subnets[*]` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CodeInterpreter.4

Untrusted IAM principal, that has been granted access to my Amazon Bedrock AgentCore code interpreter's IAM execution role through its trust policy, can assume my execution role and act with its permissions.

**Impacts:** [Data Collection](../threat-impacts.md#data-collection), [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration), [Initial Access](../threat-impacts.md#initial-access)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CodeInterpreter.2](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlcodeinterpreter2)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1048](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1048/), [T1078.004](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/004/), [T1530](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1530/)

**Scoping** (for [Identity Perimeter - Untrusted principal assumption of my IAM roles](../potential-threats.md#identity-perimeter---untrusted-principal-assumption-of-my-iam-roles)): Your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore code interpreter designates an optional IAM execution role through `$.executionRoleArn`, and you author its trust policy. That trust policy can allow identities outside your organization to assume the role and act with its permissions, such as accessing AWS resources your sessions use.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateCodeInterpreter` | `$.executionRoleArn` |
| `sts:AssumeRole` | `$.RoleArn` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CodeInterpreter.5

Threat actor, with possession of credentials for my Amazon Bedrock AgentCore code interpreter's execution role, can use my execution role while on an unexpected network.

**Impacts:** [Data Collection](../threat-impacts.md#data-collection), [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CodeInterpreter.1](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlcodeinterpreter1)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1048](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1048/), [T1530](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1530/)

**Scoping** (for [Network Perimeter - Credential use from unexpected network](../potential-threats.md#network-perimeter---credential-use-from-unexpected-network)): When you configure your code interpreter's execution role, AgentCore delivers the role's temporary credentials to sandbox code through the MicroVM Metadata Service (MMDS). A threat actor who obtains those credentials can use that execution role while on an unexpected network.

**Data perimeter:** `CreateCodeInterpreter` allows you to specify a service role, referred to as the code interpreter execution role, for your code interpreter operations. The service uses the role to make AWS API calls from your code.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `s3:GetObject` | `$.Bucket`, `$.Key` |
| `s3:PutObject` | `$.Body`, `$.Bucket`, `$.Key` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CodeInterpreter.6

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to use an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore code interpreter, can interact with the code interpreter without a record of their activities being persisted by application log delivery to Amazon CloudWatch Logs.

**Impacts:** [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CodeInterpreter.7](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlcodeinterpreter7)

**Scoping** (for [Defense evasion through unconfigured logging](../potential-threats.md#defense-evasion-through-unconfigured-logging)): When application log delivery is not configured on your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore code interpreter, no application logs are written by application log delivery to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. An IAM principal with permissions to use the code interpreter can run code, shell commands, and file operations, leaving no record of those tool invocations persisted by application log delivery.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeCodeInterpreter` | `$.arguments.code`, `$.arguments.command` |
| `bedrock-agentcore:StartCodeInterpreterSession` | *(any parameter)* |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateCodeInterpreter` | *(any parameter)* |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CodeInterpreter.7

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore code interpreter's CloudWatch Logs delivery, can disable application log delivery for the code interpreter.

**Impacts:** [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CodeInterpreter.7](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlcodeinterpreter7)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1562.008](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/008/)

**Scoping** (for [Logging disablement](../potential-threats.md#logging-disablement)): An IAM principal with permissions to modify your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore code interpreter's CloudWatch Logs delivery can delete that delivery with `DeleteDelivery` or overwrite its delivery source's `$.logType` with `PutDeliverySource`. Either change stops your code interpreter's opt-in application logs from reaching CloudWatch Logs, Amazon S3, or Amazon Data Firehose while its sessions keep running code and commands.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `cloudwatch-logs:DeleteDelivery` | `$.id` |
| `cloudwatch-logs:DeleteDeliverySource` | `$.name` |
| `cloudwatch-logs:PutDeliverySource` | `$.logType`, `$.name` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CodeInterpreter.8

Threat actor, with control of an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore code interpreter configured with overly permissive outbound security group rules, can use the code interpreter to interact with ungoverned network destinations.

**Impacts:** [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration), [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CodeInterpreter.6](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlcodeinterpreter6)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1048](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1048/)

**Scoping** (for [Data exfiltration through overly-permissive outbound security group rules](../potential-threats.md#data-exfiltration-through-overly-permissive-outbound-security-group-rules)): For an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore code interpreter in VPC network mode, outbound rules on the security groups you specify at creation govern its connections from network interfaces in your subnets. Where those rules permit an unrestricted destination range, a threat actor controlling the code interpreter can use it to interact with ungoverned network destinations.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeCodeInterpreter` | `$.arguments.code`, `$.arguments.command`, `$.x-amzn-code-interpreter-session-id` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.ConfigurationBundle.1

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create or modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore configuration bundle's component configuration, can encrypt the stored system prompts, model IDs, and tool descriptions with key material outside the AWS account owner's control.

**Impacts:** [Data Encrypted for Impact](../threat-impacts.md#data-encrypted-for-impact), [Inhibit System Recovery](../threat-impacts.md#inhibit-system-recovery)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.ConfigurationBundle.1](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlconfigurationbundle1)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1486](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1486/), [T1490](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1490/)

**Scoping** (for [Data loss through inaccessible encryption key](../potential-threats.md#data-loss-through-inaccessible-encryption-key)): An IAM principal able to create or update your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore configuration bundle chooses the KMS key that encrypts its component configurations by setting `$.kmsKeyArn`. If that key material sits outside your control, its holder can later revoke or delete it and leave those component configurations unreadable.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateConfigurationBundle` | `$.kmsKeyArn` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateConfigurationBundle` | `$.kmsKeyArn` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.ConfigurationBundle.2

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create or modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore configuration bundle, can configure the configuration bundle without required tagging information.

**Impacts:** [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.ConfigurationBundle.2](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlconfigurationbundle2)

**Scoping** (for [Resource missing required tags](../potential-threats.md#resource-missing-required-tags)): An IAM principal with permissions to create or modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore configuration bundle can omit the required tags, leaving `$.tags{key}` unset on `CreateConfigurationBundle`. A configuration bundle left without those tags still holds your agent configuration and may fall outside ownership attribution, cost allocation, and compliance inventory.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateConfigurationBundle` | `$.tags{key}` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UntagResource` | `$.tagKeys[*]` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.ConfigurationBundle.3

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create or modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore configuration bundle's component configuration, can encrypt the component configuration with an AWS owned KMS key, limiting your ability to govern the key's policy and lifecycle and to audit key usage through CloudTrail.

**Impacts:** [Data Collection](../threat-impacts.md#data-collection), [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.ConfigurationBundle.1](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlconfigurationbundle1)

**Scoping** (for [Limited encryption governance with AWS owned or managed KMS keys](../potential-threats.md#limited-encryption-governance-with-aws-owned-or-managed-kms-keys)): An IAM principal able to create or modify your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore configuration bundle's component configuration chooses whether the AWS owned key protects it at rest. You cannot govern that key's policy or lifecycle, and the service's use of it produces no CloudTrail events in your account.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateConfigurationBundle` | `$.kmsKeyArn` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateConfigurationBundle` | `$.kmsKeyArn` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.ConfigurationBundle.4

IAM principal, with unintended IAM permissions to read system prompts, model IDs, and tool descriptions from an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore configuration bundle's component configuration that has not been encrypted at rest with a KMS customer managed key, can read plaintext system prompts, model IDs, and tool descriptions in the component configuration.

**Impacts:** [Data Collection](../threat-impacts.md#data-collection), [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.ConfigurationBundle.1](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlconfigurationbundle1)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1048](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1048/), [T1213](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1213/)
