**Scoping** (for [Unauthorized data access without customer managed KMS key encryption](../potential-threats.md#unauthorized-data-access-without-customer-managed-kms-key-encryption)): Without a customer managed key, your configuration bundle's component configurations are encrypted under an AWS owned key that you cannot audit or disable. An IAM principal holding the permission to call `GetConfigurationBundle` or `GetConfigurationBundleVersion` can read those component configurations in plaintext.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateConfigurationBundle` | `$.kmsKeyArn` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:GetConfigurationBundle` | *(any parameter)* |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:GetConfigurationBundleVersion` | *(any parameter)* |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateConfigurationBundle` | `$.kmsKeyArn` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.ConfigurationBundle.5

IAM principal, with unintended IAM permissions to read system prompts, model IDs, tool descriptions, and other key-value pairs from an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore configuration bundle's component configuration that has been encrypted with an AWS owned KMS key, can read system prompts, model IDs, tool descriptions, and other key-value pairs in the component configuration.

**Impacts:** [Data Collection](../threat-impacts.md#data-collection), [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.ConfigurationBundle.1](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlconfigurationbundle1)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1048](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1048/), [T1213](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1213/)

**Scoping** (for [Unauthorized data access through AWS owned KMS key](../potential-threats.md#unauthorized-data-access-through-aws-owned-kms-key)): By default, your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore configuration bundle's component configurations are encrypted at rest with an AWS owned key. That key type gives you no key policy to govern, no audit record of key use, and no control over the key lifecycle, so an IAM principal granted broader permissions than intended can retrieve them in plaintext.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:GetConfigurationBundle` | *(any parameter)* |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:GetConfigurationBundleVersion` | *(any parameter)* |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.ConsentPortal.1

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create or modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore consent portal, can configure the consent portal without required tagging information.

**Impacts:** [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

A consent portal left without those tags still brokers end-user OAuth consent and may fall outside ownership attribution, cost allocation, and compliance inventory.

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.ConsentPortal.2

Threat actor, with knowledge of a flawed consent portal primary identity provider configuration, can take advantage of the flawed consent portal primary identity provider configuration to gain unauthorized access to the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore consent portal.

**Impacts:** [Initial Access](../threat-impacts.md#initial-access)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.ConsentPortal.2](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlconsentportal2)

A defect in that configuration can let a threat actor gain unauthorized access to the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore consent portal.

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.ConsentPortal.3

Threat actor, with knowledge of a vulnerable OIDC identity provider that has been configured as the primary identity provider of an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore consent portal, can gain federated access to the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore consent portal and the downstream resources its end users have consented to.

**Impacts:** [Initial Access](../threat-impacts.md#initial-access)

**Protocols:** `HTTPS`

**Scoping** (for [Vulnerable identity provider problem](../potential-threats.md#vulnerable-identity-provider-problem)): An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore consent portal delegates authentication for the portal to your primary OpenID Connect identity provider through the OAuth2 credential provider you supply. If that identity provider is vulnerable, a threat actor with knowledge of the vulnerability can gain federated access to your consent portal and the downstream resources your end users have consented to.

Untrusted IAM principal, that has been granted access to my Amazon Bedrock AgentCore consent portal's IAM execution role through its trust policy, can assume my execution role and act with its permissions.

**Impacts:** [Credential Theft](../threat-impacts.md#credential-theft), [Data Collection](../threat-impacts.md#data-collection), [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration), [Initial Access](../threat-impacts.md#initial-access)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.ConsentPortal.1](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlconsentportal1)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1078.004](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/004/), [T1528](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1528/), [T1555.006](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/006/)

**Scoping** (for [Identity Perimeter - Untrusted principal assumption of my IAM roles](../potential-threats.md#identity-perimeter---untrusted-principal-assumption-of-my-iam-roles)): Your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore consent portal designates an IAM execution role through `$.executionRoleArn`, and you author its trust policy. That trust policy can allow identities outside your organization to assume the role and act with its permissions.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateConsentPortal` | `$.executionRoleArn` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Dataset.1

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore dataset, can encrypt the evaluation examples in the DRAFT and all published versions of the dataset with key material outside the AWS account owner's control.

**Impacts:** [Data Encrypted for Impact](../threat-impacts.md#data-encrypted-for-impact), [Inhibit System Recovery](../threat-impacts.md#inhibit-system-recovery)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Dataset.1](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controldataset1)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1486](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1486/)

**Scoping** (for [Data loss through inaccessible encryption key](../potential-threats.md#data-loss-through-inaccessible-encryption-key)): An IAM principal able to create your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore dataset chooses the KMS key that encrypts all its evaluation examples by setting `$.kmsKeyArn`. If that key material sits outside your control, its holder can later revoke or delete it and leave those evaluation examples unreadable.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateDataset` | `$.kmsKeyArn` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Dataset.2

A dataset left without those tags still stores versioned evaluation examples and may fall outside ownership attribution, cost allocation, and compliance inventory.

**Request parameters**

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Evaluator.4

IAM principal, with unintended IAM permissions to read LLM-as-a-judge prompts and scoring definitions from an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore evaluator's instructions and rating scale that have not been encrypted at rest with a KMS customer managed key, can read plaintext LLM-as-a-judge prompts and scoring definitions in the instructions and rating scale.

An IAM principal holding the permission to call `GetEvaluator` can read that data in plaintext.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |

IAM principal, with unintended IAM permissions to read evaluation criteria and scoring definitions from an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore evaluator's instructions and rating scale that has been encrypted with an AWS owned KMS key, can read the evaluation criteria and scoring definitions in the instructions and rating scale.

That key type gives you no key policy to govern, no audit record of key use, and no control over the key lifecycle, so an IAM principal granted broader permissions than intended can retrieve them in plaintext.

| Operation | Parameters |

| `bedrock-agentcore-control:GetEvaluator` | `$.includedData` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.1

My IAM principal, with IAM permissions to configure my Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway, can configure my gateway to use an untrusted identity provider to fetch the authorization server metadata and public keys used to validate the JWT bearer tokens that callers present to invoke the gateway targets.

**Impacts:** [Data Collection](../threat-impacts.md#data-collection), [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration), [Initial Access](../threat-impacts.md#initial-access)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.9](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlgateway9)

**Scoping** (for [Resource Configuration - Data movement through an untrusted configured target](../potential-threats.md#resource-configuration---data-movement-through-an-untrusted-configured-target)): An IAM principal that creates or modifies your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway can set its custom JWT authorizer's discovery URL to an identity provider outside your organization or outside AWS. The gateway fetches that provider's authorization server metadata and public keys to validate the bearer tokens that callers present to invoke its targets.

**Data perimeter:** `CreateGateway` allows you to specify an external JWT authorizer as the value for the `authorizerConfiguration` request parameter. Because the subsequent requests against the external JWT authorizer are not governed by IAM, they are not restricted with `aws:ResourceOrgID` implemented in a service control policy.

**Data perimeter:** `UpdateGateway` allows you to specify an external JWT authorizer as the value for the `authorizerConfiguration` request parameter. Because the subsequent requests against the external JWT authorizer are not governed by IAM, they are not restricted with `aws:ResourceOrgID` implemented in a service control policy.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateGateway` | `$.authorizerConfiguration.customJWTAuthorizer.discoveryUrl` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateGateway` | `$.authorizerConfiguration.customJWTAuthorizer.discoveryUrl` |

If that key material sits outside your control, its holder can later revoke or delete it and leave that gateway data unreadable.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateGateway` | `$.kmsKeyArn` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateGateway` | `$.kmsKeyArn` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.4

Threat actor, with knowledge of a flawed inbound gateway custom JWT authorizer configuration, can take advantage of the flawed inbound gateway custom JWT authorizer configuration to gain unauthorized access to the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway and its connected targets.

**Impacts:** [Initial Access](../threat-impacts.md#initial-access)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.5](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlgateway5), [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.12](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlgateway12)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1190](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/)

**Protocols:** `HTTPS`, `MCP`

**Scoping** (for [Flawed authentication model problem](../potential-threats.md#flawed-authentication-model-problem)): The inbound custom JWT authorizer configuration of your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway admits callers to its tools and targets when their bearer tokens pass the issuer and claim rules you configure. A defect in that configuration can let a threat actor gain unauthorized access to the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway and its connected targets.

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.5

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create or modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway, can encrypt its data at rest with an AWS owned KMS key, limiting your ability to govern the key's policy and lifecycle and to audit key usage through CloudTrail.

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.4](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlgateway4)

**Scoping** (for [Limited encryption governance with AWS owned or managed KMS keys](../potential-threats.md#limited-encryption-governance-with-aws-owned-or-managed-kms-keys)): An IAM principal able to create or modify your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway chooses whether the AWS owned key protects its data at rest. You cannot govern that key's policy or lifecycle, and the service's use of it produces no CloudTrail events in your account.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateGateway` | `$.kmsKeyArn` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateGateway` | `$.kmsKeyArn` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.6

Threat actor, with a method for enumerating public Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateways, or prior knowledge of an existing public Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway, can access an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway that has been configured to allow public access.

**Impacts:** [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration), [Initial Access](../threat-impacts.md#initial-access)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.7](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlgateway7), [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.8](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlgateway8)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1048](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1048/), [T1190](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/)

**Protocols:** `HTTPS`, `MCP`

**Scoping** (for [Unintended public resource access](../potential-threats.md#unintended-public-resource-access)): An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway can be configured to allow public access through the `NONE` or `AUTHENTICATE_ONLY` authorizer type, or, with IAM authorization, a resource-based policy that grants `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeGateway` to any AWS account. A threat actor with knowledge of such an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway can then send MCP requests over HTTPS to call its tools and read the data its targets return.

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.7

IAM principal, with unintended IAM permissions to read data associated with the gateway, S3 vectors used for semantic search, and Gateway CloudWatch logs from an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway where the service uses grant-based KMS authorization, can read data associated with the gateway, S3 vectors used for semantic search, and Gateway CloudWatch logs in the gateway because the KMS key policy cannot restrict which IAM principals can decrypt the data.

**Impacts:** [Data Collection](../threat-impacts.md#data-collection), [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.2](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlgateway2), [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.10](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlgateway10)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1048](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1048/)

**Protocols:** `HTTPS`

**Scoping** (for [Unauthorized data access through service-managed KMS grants](../potential-threats.md#unauthorized-data-access-through-service-managed-kms-grants)): Amazon Bedrock AgentCore decrypts your data associated with the gateway under a KMS grant it holds, Amazon S3 Vectors decrypts your S3 vectors used for semantic search under a KMS grant it holds, and Amazon CloudWatch Logs decrypts your Gateway CloudWatch logs under its own service identity before delivery, so the key policy cannot restrict which principals read them. A customer managed key gives you audit trails, key lifecycle control, and control over key availability, not a per-principal gate on reading the data.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:GetGateway` | *(any parameter)* |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:ListGateways` | *(any parameter)* |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.8

My IAM principal, with IAM permissions on an untrusted Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway, can interact with the untrusted Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway, including sending data to it or receiving data from it.

**Impacts:** [Data Collection](../threat-impacts.md#data-collection), [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.3](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlgateway3)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1537](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1537/)

**Protocols:** `MCP`, `HTTPS`

**Scoping** (for [Resource Perimeter - Data exfiltration to untrusted resource](../potential-threats.md#resource-perimeter---data-exfiltration-to-untrusted-resource)): An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway in an account outside your organization can grant your principals access through its resource-based policy. When your principals' identity-based policies also grant that access, they can send data to that gateway or receive data from it.

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.9

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway's identity provider private endpoint, can create the identity provider private endpoint with its elastic network interfaces in a single Availability Zone.

**Impacts:** [Endpoint Denial of Service](../threat-impacts.md#endpoint-denial-of-service)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.6](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlgateway6)

**Scoping** (for [Service disruption from single availability zone dependency](../potential-threats.md#service-disruption-from-single-availability-zone-dependency)): An IAM principal with permissions to create an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway's identity provider private endpoint can use `$.authorizerConfiguration.customJWTAuthorizer.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.subnetIds[*]` to place all of the endpoint's network interfaces in a single Availability Zone. An impairment of that zone can then cut the gateway off from your identity provider's OIDC discovery and JWKS endpoints and interrupt JWT validation for the agents that call the gateway.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateGateway` | `$.authorizerConfiguration.customJWTAuthorizer.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.subnetIds[*]` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateGateway` | `$.authorizerConfiguration.customJWTAuthorizer.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.subnetIds[*]` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.10

IAM principal, with IAM permissions on my Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway and access to an unexpected network, can interact with my gateway from an unexpected network.

**Impacts:** [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration), [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion), [Initial Access](../threat-impacts.md#initial-access)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.2](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlgateway2)

**Protocols:** `HTTPS`, `MCP`

**Scoping** (for [Network Perimeter - Resource access from unexpected network](../potential-threats.md#network-perimeter---resource-access-from-unexpected-network)): An IAM principal can send requests to your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway through its public AWS-managed endpoint or an interface VPC endpoint (powered by AWS PrivateLink) for MCP traffic. An IAM principal with permissions on your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway can send it MCP requests over HTTPS or call `UpdateGateway`, `DeleteGateway`, or `PutResourcePolicy` on it from an unexpected network.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:DeleteGateway` | *(any parameter)* |

| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateGateway` | *(any parameter)* |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.11

Untrusted IAM principal, that has been granted access to my Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway through its resource-based policy, can use my gateway.

**Impacts:** [Data Collection](../threat-impacts.md#data-collection), [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration), [Initial Access](../threat-impacts.md#initial-access)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.10](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlgateway10)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1078.004](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/004/)

**Protocols:** `HTTPS`, `MCP`

**Scoping** (for [Identity Perimeter - Untrusted principal access to my resources](../potential-threats.md#identity-perimeter---untrusted-principal-access-to-my-resources)): The resource-based policy on your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway can grant `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeGateway` access to principals outside your organization. When your gateway uses IAM (SigV4) inbound authorization, such a principal can call the gateway's tools and targets with its own credentials. That principal may then reach your backend data through the IAM execution role, OAuth tokens, or API keys your gateway uses for those calls.

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.12

Threat actor, with knowledge of a vulnerable OAuth 2.0 authorization server or OIDC identity provider that has been configured in the custom JWT authorizer of an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway, can gain federated access to the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway and the tools and targets behind it.

**Impacts:** [Initial Access](../threat-impacts.md#initial-access)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.5](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlgateway5), [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.12](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlgateway12)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1190](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/)

**Protocols:** `HTTPS`

**Scoping** (for [Vulnerable identity provider problem](../potential-threats.md#vulnerable-identity-provider-problem)): An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway delegates authentication for its gateway URL to an external OAuth 2.0 authorization server or OIDC identity provider through the custom JWT authorizer you configure. If that identity provider is vulnerable, a threat actor presenting a forged or replayed JWT can gain federated access to the tools and targets behind your gateway.

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.13

Untrusted IAM principal, that has been granted access to my Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway's IAM service role through its trust policy, can assume my service role and act with its permissions.

**Impacts:** [Credential Theft](../threat-impacts.md#credential-theft), [Data Collection](../threat-impacts.md#data-collection), [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration), [Initial Access](../threat-impacts.md#initial-access)

**Scoping** (for [Identity Perimeter - Untrusted principal assumption of my IAM roles](../potential-threats.md#identity-perimeter---untrusted-principal-assumption-of-my-iam-roles)): Your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway designates an IAM service role through `$.roleArn`, and you author its trust policy. That trust policy can allow identities outside your organization to assume the role and act with its permissions.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateGateway` | `$.roleArn` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateGateway` | `$.roleArn` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.14

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to use an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway, can interact with the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway without a record of their activities being persisted by vended log delivery.

**Impacts:** [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.15](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlgateway15)

**Protocols:** `MCP`, `HTTPS`

**Scoping** (for [Defense evasion through unconfigured logging](../potential-threats.md#defense-evasion-through-unconfigured-logging)): When vended log delivery is not configured on your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway, no vended logs are written by vended log delivery. An IAM principal with permissions to use the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway can list and call its MCP tools, leaving no record of those MCP requests persisted by vended log delivery.

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.15

Untrusted IAM principal, with access to configure an AWS service that has been granted access to an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway through its resource-based policy, may be able to cause that AWS service to interact with the gateway using the principal's data or context.

**Impacts:** [Privilege Escalation](../threat-impacts.md#privilege-escalation)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.11](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlgateway11)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1548.005](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1548/005/)

**Scoping** (for [Cross-service confused deputy problem through resource-based policies](../potential-threats.md#cross-service-confused-deputy-problem-through-resource-based-policies)): Your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway's resource-based policy can grant access to an AWS service. An untrusted IAM principal who can configure that service may cause it to interact with your gateway using their own data or context.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:PutResourcePolicy` | `$.policy` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.16

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway, can disable vended log delivery of application logs and traces for the gateway.

**Impacts:** [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.15](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlgateway15)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1562.008](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/008/)

**Scoping** (for [Logging disablement](../potential-threats.md#logging-disablement)): An IAM principal with permissions to modify your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway can delete its log deliveries and delivery sources with `DeleteDelivery` and `DeleteDeliverySource`. Deleting them stops the gateway's opt-in application logs and trace spans from reaching CloudWatch Logs while later `InvokeGateway` activity goes unrecorded; deleting only the `APPLICATION_LOGS` delivery stops application logs but not `TRACES` spans.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `cloudwatch-logs:DeleteDelivery` | `$.id` |
| `cloudwatch-logs:DeleteDeliverySource` | `$.name` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.17

Threat actor, with control of an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway's identity provider private endpoint configured with overly permissive outbound security group rules, can use the identity provider private endpoint to interact with ungoverned network destinations.

**Impacts:** [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration), [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.14](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlgateway14)

**Protocols:** `HTTPS`

**Scoping** (for [Data exfiltration through overly-permissive outbound security group rules](../potential-threats.md#data-exfiltration-through-overly-permissive-outbound-security-group-rules)): The outbound rules of the security groups you specify for your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway's identity provider private endpoint govern outbound connections from its network interfaces in your subnets. Where those rules permit an unrestricted destination range, a threat actor controlling the gateway's identity provider private endpoint can use it to interact with ungoverned network destinations.

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.GatewayTarget.1

My IAM principal, with IAM permissions to configure my Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway target, can configure my gateway target to use an untrusted HTTP endpoint to exchange tool call, agent, and model inference traffic, including any outbound credentials the gateway injects.

**Impacts:** [Credential Theft](../threat-impacts.md#credential-theft), [Data Collection](../threat-impacts.md#data-collection), [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.GatewayTarget.4](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlgatewaytarget4)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1119](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1119/), [T1528](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1528/)

**Scoping** (for [Resource Configuration - Data movement through an untrusted configured target](../potential-threats.md#resource-configuration---data-movement-through-an-untrusted-configured-target)): An IAM principal that creates or modifies your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway target can set its target configuration to an HTTP endpoint outside your organization or outside AWS. The gateway then exchanges tool call, agent, and model inference traffic with that endpoint, including any outbound credentials it injects.

**Data perimeter:** `CreateGatewayTarget` allows you to specify an HTTP endpoint as the value for the `targetConfiguration` request parameter. Because the subsequent requests against the HTTP endpoint are not governed by IAM, they are not restricted with `aws:ResourceOrgID` implemented in a service control policy.

**Data perimeter:** `UpdateGatewayTarget` allows you to specify an HTTP endpoint as the value for the `targetConfiguration` request parameter. Because the subsequent requests against the HTTP endpoint are not governed by IAM, they are not restricted with `aws:ResourceOrgID` implemented in a service control policy.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateGatewayTarget` | `$.targetConfiguration.http.passthrough.endpoint`, `$.targetConfiguration.inference.provider.endpoint`, `$.targetConfiguration.mcp.mcpServer.endpoint`, `$.targetConfiguration.mcp.openApiSchema.inlinePayload`, `$.targetConfiguration.mcp.openApiSchema.s3.uri` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateGatewayTarget` | `$.targetConfiguration.http.passthrough.endpoint`, `$.targetConfiguration.inference.provider.endpoint`, `$.targetConfiguration.mcp.mcpServer.endpoint`, `$.targetConfiguration.mcp.openApiSchema.inlinePayload`, `$.targetConfiguration.mcp.openApiSchema.s3.uri` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.GatewayTarget.2

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway target that is not attached to a VPC, can use the gateway target to send and receive traffic outside the network controls a VPC would enforce.

**Impacts:** [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration), [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion), [Lateral Movement](../threat-impacts.md#lateral-movement)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.GatewayTarget.2](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlgatewaytarget2)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1048](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1048/)

**Scoping** (for [Ungoverned network traffic from non-VPC resources](../potential-threats.md#ungoverned-network-traffic-from-non-vpc-resources)): Your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway target does not run in your VPCs when its `privateEndpoint` setting is omitted. An IAM principal with create permissions can then use it to send and receive traffic outside the network controls a VPC would enforce, reaching the host set in its backend endpoint or schema server URL.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateGatewayTarget` | `$.targetConfiguration.http.passthrough.endpoint`, `$.targetConfiguration.inference.provider.endpoint`, `$.targetConfiguration.mcp.mcpServer.endpoint`, `$.targetConfiguration.mcp.openApiSchema.inlinePayload`, `$.targetConfiguration.mcp.openApiSchema.s3.uri`, `$.targetConfiguration.mcp.smithyModel.inlinePayload`, `$.targetConfiguration.mcp.smithyModel.s3.uri` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:SynchronizeGatewayTargets` | `$.targetIdList[*]` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateGatewayTarget` | `$.targetConfiguration.http.passthrough.endpoint`, `$.targetConfiguration.inference.provider.endpoint`, `$.targetConfiguration.mcp.mcpServer.endpoint`, `$.targetConfiguration.mcp.openApiSchema.inlinePayload`, `$.targetConfiguration.mcp.openApiSchema.s3.uri`, `$.targetConfiguration.mcp.smithyModel.inlinePayload`, `$.targetConfiguration.mcp.smithyModel.s3.uri` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.GatewayTarget.3

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway target's private endpoint, can create the private endpoint with its elastic network interfaces in a single Availability Zone.

**Impacts:** [Endpoint Denial of Service](../threat-impacts.md#endpoint-denial-of-service)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.GatewayTarget.3](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlgatewaytarget3)

**Scoping** (for [Service disruption from single availability zone dependency](../potential-threats.md#service-disruption-from-single-availability-zone-dependency)): An IAM principal with permissions to create an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway target's private endpoint can set `$.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.subnetIds[*]` to place the endpoint's network interfaces in a single Availability Zone. An impairment of that zone can then make the private endpoint unreachable and interrupt the tool calls and proxied requests that agents send to the target.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateGatewayTarget` | `$.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.subnetIds[*]` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateGatewayTarget` | `$.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.subnetIds[*]` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.GatewayTarget.4

Threat actor, with network access to an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway target's private endpoint that has been placed in a public subnet, can access the private endpoint directly from an ungoverned network.

**Impacts:** [Account and Resource Discovery](../threat-impacts.md#account-and-resource-discovery), [Initial Access](../threat-impacts.md#initial-access)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.GatewayTarget.1](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlgatewaytarget1)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1190](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/)

**Protocols:** `HTTPS`

**Scoping** (for [Public subnet resource exposure](../potential-threats.md#public-subnet-resource-exposure)): An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway target's private endpoint places the network interfaces of an AgentCore-managed VPC Lattice resource gateway in the subnets you choose for it. An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway target's private endpoint placed in a subnet that routes to an internet gateway can be reached directly from an ungoverned network when those interfaces have a public IP address.

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.GatewayTarget.5

Threat actor, with control of an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway target configured with overly permissive outbound security group rules, can use the gateway target to interact with ungoverned network destinations.

| `bedrock-agentcore-control:SynchronizeGatewayTargets` | `$.targetIdList[*]` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Harness.1

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness that is not attached to a VPC, can use the harness to send and receive traffic outside the network controls a VPC would enforce.

**Impacts:** [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration), [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion), [Lateral Movement](../threat-impacts.md#lateral-movement)

**Scoping** (for [Ungoverned network traffic from non-VPC resources](../potential-threats.md#ungoverned-network-traffic-from-non-vpc-resources)): Your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness does not run in your VPCs when `$.environment.agentCoreRuntimeEnvironment.networkConfiguration.networkMode` is `PUBLIC` or omitted. An IAM principal with create permissions can then use it to send and receive traffic outside the network controls a VPC would enforce, reaching remote MCP servers, Git skill repositories, model provider endpoints and other public internet hosts.

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Harness.2

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create or modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness's managed memory, can encrypt the conversation events and long-term memory records with key material outside the AWS account owner's control.

**Impacts:** [Data Encrypted for Impact](../threat-impacts.md#data-encrypted-for-impact), [Inhibit System Recovery](../threat-impacts.md#inhibit-system-recovery)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Harness.4](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlharness4)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1486](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1486/)

**Scoping** (for [Data loss through inaccessible encryption key](../potential-threats.md#data-loss-through-inaccessible-encryption-key)): An IAM principal able to create or update your harness chooses the KMS key that encrypts its managed memory data by setting `$.memory.managedMemoryConfiguration.encryptionKeyArn` at creation and `$.memory.optionalValue.managedMemoryConfiguration.encryptionKeyArn` on update. If that key material sits outside your control, its holder can later revoke or delete it and leave that memory data unreadable.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateHarness` | `$.memory.managedMemoryConfiguration.encryptionKeyArn` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateHarness` | `$.memory.optionalValue.managedMemoryConfiguration.encryptionKeyArn` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Harness.3

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create or modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness, can configure the harness without required tagging information.

**Impacts:** [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Harness.7](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlharness7)

**Scoping** (for [Resource missing required tags](../potential-threats.md#resource-missing-required-tags)): An IAM principal with permissions to create or modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness can omit the required tags, or remove them later through `UntagResource`. A harness left without those tags still runs agent sessions and may fall outside ownership attribution, cost allocation, and compliance inventory.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateHarness` | `$.tags{key}` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UntagResource` | `$.tagKeys[*]` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Harness.4

Threat actor, with knowledge of a flawed inbound harness custom JWT authorizer configuration, can take advantage of the flawed inbound harness custom JWT authorizer configuration to gain unauthorized access to the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness.

**Impacts:** [Initial Access](../threat-impacts.md#initial-access)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Harness.6](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlharness6)

**Scoping** (for [Flawed authentication model problem](../potential-threats.md#flawed-authentication-model-problem)): The inbound custom JWT authorizer configuration of your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness lets callers invoke it with bearer tokens that pass the issuer and claim checks you configure. A defect in that authorizer configuration can let a threat actor gain unauthorized access to the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeHarness` | `$.qualifier` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Harness.5

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create or modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness's managed memory, can encrypt the managed memory with an AWS owned KMS key, limiting your ability to govern the key's policy and lifecycle and to audit key usage through CloudTrail.

**Impacts:** [Data Collection](../threat-impacts.md#data-collection), [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Harness.4](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlharness4)

**Scoping** (for [Limited encryption governance with AWS owned or managed KMS keys](../potential-threats.md#limited-encryption-governance-with-aws-owned-or-managed-kms-keys)): An IAM principal able to create or modify your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness's managed memory chooses whether the AWS owned key protects its conversation events and long-term memory records at rest. You cannot govern that key's policy or lifecycle, and the service's use of it produces no CloudTrail events in your account.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateHarness` | `$.memory.managedMemoryConfiguration.encryptionKeyArn` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateHarness` | `$.memory.optionalValue.managedMemoryConfiguration.encryptionKeyArn` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Harness.6

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness, can create the harness with its elastic network interfaces in a single Availability Zone.

An impairment of that zone can then leave those sessions without a network path and interrupt `InvokeHarness` calls from your authorized callers.

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Memory.2

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create or modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore memory, can configure the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore memory without required tagging information.

**Impacts:** [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Memory.4](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlmemory4)

**Scoping** (for [Resource missing required tags](../potential-threats.md#resource-missing-required-tags)): An IAM principal with permissions to create or modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore memory can omit the required tags, or remove them later through `UntagResource`. An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore memory left without those tags still stores agent conversation data and may fall outside ownership attribution, cost allocation, and compliance inventory.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateMemory` | `$.tags{key}` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UntagResource` | `$.tagKeys[*]` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Memory.3

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore memory, can encrypt its short-term events and long-term memory records with an AWS owned KMS key, limiting your ability to govern the key's policy and lifecycle and to audit key usage through CloudTrail.

**Impacts:** [Data Collection](../threat-impacts.md#data-collection), [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Memory.3](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlmemory3)

**Scoping** (for [Limited encryption governance with AWS owned or managed KMS keys](../potential-threats.md#limited-encryption-governance-with-aws-owned-or-managed-kms-keys)): An IAM principal able to create your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore memory chooses whether the AWS owned key protects its short-term events and long-term memory records at rest. You cannot govern that key's policy or lifecycle, and the service's use of it produces no CloudTrail events in your account.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateMemory` | `$.encryptionKeyArn` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Memory.4

My IAM principal, with IAM permissions on an untrusted Amazon Bedrock AgentCore memory, can interact with the untrusted memory, including sending data to it or receiving data from it.

**Impacts:** [Data Collection](../threat-impacts.md#data-collection), [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Memory.2](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlmemory2)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1537](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1537/)

**Scoping** (for [Resource Perimeter - Data exfiltration to untrusted resource](../potential-threats.md#resource-perimeter---data-exfiltration-to-untrusted-resource)): An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore memory in an account outside your organization can grant your principals access through a resource-based policy. Your principals with IAM permissions on that memory can then write content into it by calling `CreateEvent` or `BatchCreateMemoryRecords`. They can also receive records that the memory's owner controls by calling `RetrieveMemoryRecords`.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore:BatchCreateMemoryRecords` | `$.records[*].content.text` |
| `bedrock-agentcore:CreateEvent` | `$.payload[*].blob`, `$.payload[*].conversational.content.text`, `$.payload[*].json.content` |
| `bedrock-agentcore:RetrieveMemoryRecords` | *(any parameter)* |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Memory.5

Untrusted IAM principal, that has been granted access to my Amazon Bedrock AgentCore memory's IAM execution role through its trust policy, can assume my execution role and act with its permissions.

**Impacts:** [Data Collection](../threat-impacts.md#data-collection), [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration), [Initial Access](../threat-impacts.md#initial-access), [Resource Hijacking](../threat-impacts.md#resource-hijacking)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Memory.1](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlmemory1)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1048](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1048/), [T1078.004](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/004/), [T1496.004](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1496/004/), [T1530](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1530/)

**Scoping** (for [Identity Perimeter - Untrusted principal assumption of my IAM roles](../potential-threats.md#identity-perimeter---untrusted-principal-assumption-of-my-iam-roles)): Your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore memory designates an optional execution role through `$.memoryExecutionRoleArn`, and you author its trust policy. That trust policy can allow identities outside your organization to assume the role and act with its permissions.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateMemory` | `$.memoryExecutionRoleArn` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateMemory` | `$.memoryExecutionRoleArn` |
| `sts:AssumeRole` | `$.RoleArn` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Memory.6

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to use an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore memory, can interact with the memory without a record of their activities being persisted by APPLICATION_LOGS and TRACES vended log delivery.

**Impacts:** [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Memory.5](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlmemory5)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1078.004](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/004/)

**Scoping** (for [Defense evasion through unconfigured logging](../potential-threats.md#defense-evasion-through-unconfigured-logging)): When application log delivery and trace delivery are not configured on your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore memory, no application logs or traces are written by application log delivery and trace delivery. An IAM principal with permissions to use the memory can interact with the memory, leaving no record of those interactions persisted by application log delivery and trace delivery.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore:CreateEvent` | `$.actorId`, `$.payload[*].conversational.content.text`, `$.sessionId` |
| `bedrock-agentcore:DeleteEvent` | `$.eventId` |
| `bedrock-agentcore:GetEvent` | `$.eventId` |
| `bedrock-agentcore:ListEvents` | `$.includePayloads` |
| `bedrock-agentcore:ListMemoryRecords` | `$.namespacePath` |
| `bedrock-agentcore:RetrieveMemoryRecords` | `$.namespace`, `$.namespacePath` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Memory.7

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore memory, can disable vended logs delivery of APPLICATION_LOGS and TRACES for the memory.

**Impacts:** [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Memory.5](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlmemory5)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1562.008](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/008/)

**Scoping** (for [Logging disablement](../potential-threats.md#logging-disablement)): An IAM principal with permissions to modify your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore memory can delete its log deliveries with `DeleteDelivery` and then its delivery sources with `DeleteDeliverySource`. Deleting them stops the memory's opt-in application logs and traces from reaching CloudWatch Logs while event writes, record retrievals and memory deletion leave no such entries; `DeleteDelivery` on only the traces delivery stops spans and leaves application logs flowing.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `cloudwatch-logs:DeleteDelivery` | `$.id` |
| `cloudwatch-logs:DeleteDeliverySource` | `$.name` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Oauth2CredentialProvider.1

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create or modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore OAuth2 credential provider, can configure the OAuth2 credential provider without required tagging information.

**Impacts:** [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Oauth2CredentialProvider.3](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controloauth2credentialprovider3)

**Scoping** (for [Resource missing required tags](../potential-threats.md#resource-missing-required-tags)): An IAM principal with permissions to create or modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore OAuth2 credential provider can omit the required tags, by leaving out `$.tags{key}` on `CreateOauth2CredentialProvider`. An OAuth2 credential provider left without those tags still brokers OAuth tokens for agents and may fall outside ownership attribution, cost allocation, and compliance inventory.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateOauth2CredentialProvider` | `$.tags{key}` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Oauth2CredentialProvider.2

Threat actor, with knowledge of a flawed OAuth 2.0 provider configuration of an OAuth2 credential provider, can take advantage of the flawed OAuth 2.0 provider configuration of an OAuth2 credential provider to gain unauthorized access to the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore OAuth2 credential provider.

**Impacts:** [Initial Access](../threat-impacts.md#initial-access)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Oauth2CredentialProvider.2](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controloauth2credentialprovider2)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1078.004](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/004/)

**Scoping** (for [Flawed authentication model problem](../potential-threats.md#flawed-authentication-model-problem)): Through its OAuth 2.0 provider configuration, your OAuth2 credential provider maps agent and end-user identities to tokens from the authorization server it trusts. A defect in that configuration can let a threat actor gain unauthorized access to the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore OAuth2 credential provider.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore:CompleteResourceTokenAuth` | `$.sessionUri`, `$.userIdentifier.userId`, `$.userIdentifier.userToken` |
| `bedrock-agentcore:GetResourceOauth2Token` | `$.audiences[*]`, `$.oauth2Flow`, `$.resourceOauth2ReturnUrl`, `$.scopes[*]`, `$.sessionUri`, `$.workloadIdentityToken` |
| `bedrock-agentcore:GetWorkloadAccessTokenForJWT` | `$.userToken` |
| `sts:GetWebIdentityToken` | `$.Audience[*]` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Oauth2CredentialProvider.3

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create or modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore OAuth2 credential provider's private endpoint, can create the private endpoint with its elastic network interfaces in a single Availability Zone.

**Impacts:** [Endpoint Denial of Service](../threat-impacts.md#endpoint-denial-of-service)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Oauth2CredentialProvider.1](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controloauth2credentialprovider1)

**Scoping** (for [Service disruption from single availability zone dependency](../potential-threats.md#service-disruption-from-single-availability-zone-dependency)): An IAM principal with permissions to create or modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore OAuth2 credential provider's private endpoint can set `$.oauth2ProviderConfigInput.customOauth2ProviderConfig.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.subnetIds[*]` or `$.oauth2ProviderConfigInput.customOauth2ProviderConfig.privateEndpointOverrides[*].privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.subnetIds[*]` to place the managed Amazon VPC Lattice resource gateway's network interfaces in a single Availability Zone. An impairment of that zone can then make the private endpoint unreachable and stop your agents, gateway targets, and harnesses that use this provider from obtaining new or refreshed tokens.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateOauth2CredentialProvider` | `$.oauth2ProviderConfigInput.customOauth2ProviderConfig.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.subnetIds[*]`, `$.oauth2ProviderConfigInput.customOauth2ProviderConfig.privateEndpointOverrides[*].privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.subnetIds[*]` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateOauth2CredentialProvider` | `$.oauth2ProviderConfigInput.customOauth2ProviderConfig.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.subnetIds[*]`, `$.oauth2ProviderConfigInput.customOauth2ProviderConfig.privateEndpointOverrides[*].privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.subnetIds[*]` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Oauth2CredentialProvider.4

Threat actor, with knowledge of a vulnerable OAuth 2.0 identity provider that has been configured in an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore OAuth2 credential provider, can gain federated access to the resource servers the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore OAuth2 credential provider obtains tokens for.

**Impacts:** [Initial Access](../threat-impacts.md#initial-access)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Oauth2CredentialProvider.2](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controloauth2credentialprovider2)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1190](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/)

**Scoping** (for [Vulnerable identity provider problem](../potential-threats.md#vulnerable-identity-provider-problem)): An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore OAuth2 credential provider delegates authentication for your agents' outbound access to resource servers to the external OAuth 2.0 identity provider named by its vendor and provider configuration. If that identity provider is vulnerable, a threat actor presenting a replayed or forged token can gain federated access to the resource servers your OAuth2 credential provider obtains tokens for.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore:CompleteResourceTokenAuth` | `$.sessionUri`, `$.userIdentifier.userToken` |
| `bedrock-agentcore:GetResourceOauth2Token` | `$.customParameters{key}`, `$.oauth2Flow`, `$.sessionUri`, `$.workloadIdentityToken` |
| `bedrock-agentcore:GetWorkloadAccessTokenForJWT` | `$.userToken` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Oauth2CredentialProvider.5

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to use an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore OAuth2 credential provider, can interact with the OAuth2 credential provider without a record of their activities being persisted by trace delivery.

**Impacts:** [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Oauth2CredentialProvider.5](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controloauth2credentialprovider5)

**Scoping** (for [Defense evasion through unconfigured logging](../potential-threats.md#defense-evasion-through-unconfigured-logging)): When trace delivery is not configured on your OAuth2 credential provider, no traces are written by trace delivery. An IAM principal with permissions to use the OAuth2 credential provider can interact with it, leaving no record of those interactions persisted by trace delivery.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore:GetResourceOauth2Token` | `$.oauth2Flow`, `$.scopes[*]`, `$.workloadIdentityToken` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Oauth2CredentialProvider.6

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore OAuth2 credential provider, can disable vended log delivery of traces for the OAuth2 credential provider.

**Impacts:** [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Oauth2CredentialProvider.5](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controloauth2credentialprovider5)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1562.008](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/008/)

**Scoping** (for [Logging disablement](../potential-threats.md#logging-disablement)): An IAM principal with permissions to modify your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore OAuth2 credential provider can delete its log delivery with `DeleteDelivery`, then its delivery source with `DeleteDeliverySource`. Deleting the delivery stops the provider's opt-in AgentCore Identity trace spans from reaching CloudWatch Logs while `GetResourceOauth2Token` calls continue without those records.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `cloudwatch-logs:DeleteDelivery` | `$.id` |
| `cloudwatch-logs:DeleteDeliverySource` | `$.name` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Oauth2CredentialProvider.7

Threat actor, with control of an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore OAuth2 credential provider configured with overly permissive outbound security group rules, can use the OAuth2 credential provider to interact with ungoverned network destinations.

**Impacts:** [Credential Theft](../threat-impacts.md#credential-theft), [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration), [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Oauth2CredentialProvider.4](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controloauth2credentialprovider4)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1048](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1048/), [T1528](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1528/)

**Scoping** (for [Data exfiltration through overly-permissive outbound security group rules](../potential-threats.md#data-exfiltration-through-overly-permissive-outbound-security-group-rules)): The security groups you specify for the OAuth2 credential provider's managed private endpoint, or otherwise your VPC's default security group, attach to its resource gateway's network interfaces in your subnets, where the connections to the discovery URL, token endpoint, override domains or routing domain set on the provider originate. Where those rules permit an unrestricted destination range, a threat actor controlling the OAuth2 credential provider can use it to interact with ungoverned network destinations.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore:GetResourceOauth2Token` | `$.customParameters{key}`, `$.forceAuthentication`, `$.oauth2Flow` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateOauth2CredentialProvider` | `$.oauth2ProviderConfigInput.customOauth2ProviderConfig.oauthDiscovery.authorizationServerMetadata.tokenEndpoint`, `$.oauth2ProviderConfigInput.customOauth2ProviderConfig.oauthDiscovery.discoveryUrl`, `$.oauth2ProviderConfigInput.customOauth2ProviderConfig.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.routingDomain`, `$.oauth2ProviderConfigInput.customOauth2ProviderConfig.privateEndpointOverrides[*].domain` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateOauth2CredentialProvider` | `$.oauth2ProviderConfigInput.customOauth2ProviderConfig.oauthDiscovery.authorizationServerMetadata.tokenEndpoint`, `$.oauth2ProviderConfigInput.customOauth2ProviderConfig.oauthDiscovery.discoveryUrl`, `$.oauth2ProviderConfigInput.customOauth2ProviderConfig.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.routingDomain`, `$.oauth2ProviderConfigInput.customOauth2ProviderConfig.privateEndpointOverrides[*].domain`, `$.oauth2ProviderConfigInput.customOauth2ProviderConfig.privateEndpointOverrides[*].privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.routingDomain` |
