| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreatePaymentManager` | `$.kmsKeyArn` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdatePaymentManager` | `$.kmsKeyArn` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.PaymentManager.5

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payment manager's VPC Lattice resource gateway, can create the VPC Lattice resource gateway with its elastic network interfaces in a single Availability Zone.

**Impacts:** [Endpoint Denial of Service](../threat-impacts.md#endpoint-denial-of-service)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.PaymentManager.4](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlpaymentmanager4)

**Scoping** (for [Service disruption from single availability zone dependency](../potential-threats.md#service-disruption-from-single-availability-zone-dependency)): An IAM principal with permissions to create an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payment manager's VPC Lattice resource gateway can use the subnet list `$.authorizerConfiguration.customJWTAuthorizer.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.subnetIds[*]` on `CreatePaymentManager` or `UpdatePaymentManager` to place all of the resource gateway's network interfaces in a single Availability Zone. An impairment of that zone can then cut off AgentCore's path to your private identity provider and interrupt JWT validation for payment calls such as `ProcessPayment` that your agents make.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreatePaymentManager` | `$.authorizerConfiguration.customJWTAuthorizer.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.subnetIds[*]` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdatePaymentManager` | `$.authorizerConfiguration.customJWTAuthorizer.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.subnetIds[*]` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.PaymentManager.6

Threat actor, with knowledge of a vulnerable OIDC identity provider that has been configured in the custom JWT authorizer of an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payment manager, can gain federated access to the payments data plane of the payment manager.

**Impacts:** [Initial Access](../threat-impacts.md#initial-access)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.PaymentManager.3](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlpaymentmanager3), [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.PaymentManager.5](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlpaymentmanager5)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1078.004](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/004/)

**Scoping** (for [Vulnerable identity provider problem](../potential-threats.md#vulnerable-identity-provider-problem)): An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payment manager delegates authentication for its data plane operations to the OpenID Connect identity provider you name when you choose a custom JWT authorizer. If that identity provider is vulnerable, a threat actor presenting a signed bearer token from that provider can gain federated access to the payments data plane of your payment manager, including `CreatePaymentInstrument`, `CreatePaymentSession` and `ProcessPayment`.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore:CreatePaymentInstrument` | *(any parameter)* |
| `bedrock-agentcore:CreatePaymentSession` | *(any parameter)* |
| `bedrock-agentcore:GetPaymentInstrumentBalance` | *(any parameter)* |
| `bedrock-agentcore:ListPaymentInstruments` | *(any parameter)* |
| `bedrock-agentcore:ProcessPayment` | `$.paymentInstrumentId` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.PaymentManager.7

Untrusted IAM principal, that has been granted access to my Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payment manager's IAM service role through its trust policy, can assume my service role and act with its permissions.

**Impacts:** [Credential Theft](../threat-impacts.md#credential-theft), [Data Collection](../threat-impacts.md#data-collection), [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration), [Initial Access](../threat-impacts.md#initial-access)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.PaymentManager.1](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlpaymentmanager1)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1048](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1048/), [T1078.004](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/004/), [T1528](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1528/), [T1555.006](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/006/)

**Scoping** (for [Identity Perimeter - Untrusted principal assumption of my IAM roles](../potential-threats.md#identity-perimeter---untrusted-principal-assumption-of-my-iam-roles)): Your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payment manager designates a service role through `$.roleArn`, and you author its trust policy. That trust policy can allow identities outside your organization to assume the role and act with its permissions.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreatePaymentManager` | `$.roleArn` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdatePaymentManager` | `$.roleArn` |
| `sts:AssumeRole` | `$.RoleArn` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.PaymentManager.8

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to use an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payment manager, can interact with the payment manager without a record of their activities being persisted by vended application log delivery to CloudWatch Logs.

**Impacts:** [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.PaymentManager.8](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlpaymentmanager8)

**Scoping** (for [Defense evasion through unconfigured logging](../potential-threats.md#defense-evasion-through-unconfigured-logging)): When vended application log delivery is not configured on your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payment manager, no application logs are written by vended application log delivery to CloudWatch Logs. An IAM principal with permissions to use the payment manager can interact with the payment manager, leaving no record of those interactions persisted by vended application log delivery.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore:CreatePaymentInstrument` | *(any parameter)* |
| `bedrock-agentcore:CreatePaymentSession` | *(any parameter)* |
| `bedrock-agentcore:GetPaymentInstrumentBalance` | *(any parameter)* |
| `bedrock-agentcore:ProcessPayment` | *(any parameter)* |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.PaymentManager.9

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payment manager, can disable vended application log delivery to CloudWatch Logs for the payment manager.

**Impacts:** [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.PaymentManager.8](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlpaymentmanager8)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1562.008](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/008/)

**Scoping** (for [Logging disablement](../potential-threats.md#logging-disablement)): An IAM principal with permissions to modify your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payment manager can delete its application log delivery with `DeleteDelivery` and then its delivery source with `DeleteDeliverySource`. Deleting the delivery stops the opt-in application logs that record each data plane call from reaching CloudWatch Logs while payment calls such as `ProcessPayment` continue unrecorded.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `cloudwatch-logs:DeleteDelivery` | `$.id` |
| `cloudwatch-logs:DeleteDeliverySource` | `$.name` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.PaymentManager.10

Threat actor, with control of an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payment manager configured with overly permissive outbound security group rules, can use the payment manager to interact with ungoverned network destinations.

**Impacts:** [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration), [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.PaymentManager.7](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlpaymentmanager7)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1048](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1048/)

**Scoping** (for [Data exfiltration through overly-permissive outbound security group rules](../potential-threats.md#data-exfiltration-through-overly-permissive-outbound-security-group-rules)): When your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payment manager's custom JWT authorizer uses a managed private endpoint, the security groups you specify, or your VPC's default security group, attach to a managed VPC Lattice resource gateway in your subnets, and their outbound rules govern the connections it opens to the discovery URL or routing domain set on the payment manager. Where those rules permit an unrestricted destination range, a threat actor controlling the payment manager can use it to interact with ungoverned network destinations.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreatePaymentManager` | `$.authorizerConfiguration.customJWTAuthorizer.discoveryUrl`, `$.authorizerConfiguration.customJWTAuthorizer.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.routingDomain` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdatePaymentManager` | `$.authorizerConfiguration.customJWTAuthorizer.discoveryUrl`, `$.authorizerConfiguration.customJWTAuthorizer.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.routingDomain` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.PolicyEngine.1

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore policy engine, can encrypt the policy engine data, including policies and policy generations, with key material outside the AWS account owner's control.

**Impacts:** [Data Encrypted for Impact](../threat-impacts.md#data-encrypted-for-impact), [Inhibit System Recovery](../threat-impacts.md#inhibit-system-recovery), [Service Stop](../threat-impacts.md#service-stop)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.PolicyEngine.1](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlpolicyengine1)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1486](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1486/)

**Scoping** (for [Data loss through inaccessible encryption key](../potential-threats.md#data-loss-through-inaccessible-encryption-key)): An IAM principal able to create your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore policy engine chooses the KMS key that encrypts the policy engine data by setting `$.encryptionKeyArn`. If that key material sits outside your control, its holder can later revoke or delete it and leave that policy engine data unreadable.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreatePolicyEngine` | `$.encryptionKeyArn` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.PolicyEngine.2

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create or modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore policy engine, can configure the policy engine without required tagging information.

**Impacts:** [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.PolicyEngine.2](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlpolicyengine2)

**Scoping** (for [Resource missing required tags](../potential-threats.md#resource-missing-required-tags)): An IAM principal with permissions to create or modify an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore policy engine can omit the required tags, or remove them through `UntagResource`. A policy engine left without those tags still authorizes agent tool calls and may fall outside ownership attribution, cost allocation, and compliance inventory.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreatePolicyEngine` | `$.tags{key}` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UntagResource` | `$.tagKeys[*]` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.PolicyEngine.3

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore policy engine, can encrypt the policy engine, its policies, and its policy generations with an AWS owned KMS key, limiting your ability to govern the key's policy and lifecycle and to audit key usage through CloudTrail.

**Impacts:** [Data Collection](../threat-impacts.md#data-collection), [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.PolicyEngine.1](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlpolicyengine1)

**Scoping** (for [Limited encryption governance with AWS owned or managed KMS keys](../potential-threats.md#limited-encryption-governance-with-aws-owned-or-managed-kms-keys)): An IAM principal able to create your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore policy engine chooses whether the AWS owned key protects the engine, its policies, and its policy generations at rest. You cannot govern that key's policy or lifecycle, and the service's use of it produces no CloudTrail events in your account.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreatePolicyEngine` | `$.encryptionKeyArn` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.PolicyEngine.4

IAM principal, with unintended IAM permissions to read description, status reasons, policy definitions, and policy generation assets from an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore policy engine that has not been encrypted at rest with a KMS customer managed key, can read plaintext description, status reasons, policy definitions, and policy generation assets in the policy engine.

**Impacts:** [Data Collection](../threat-impacts.md#data-collection), [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.PolicyEngine.1](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlpolicyengine1)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1213](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1213/)

**Scoping** (for [Unauthorized data access without customer managed KMS key encryption](../potential-threats.md#unauthorized-data-access-without-customer-managed-kms-key-encryption)): Without a customer managed key, your policy engine's description, status reasons, policy definitions, and policy generation assets are encrypted under an AWS owned key that you cannot audit or disable. An IAM principal holding the permission to call `GetPolicyEngine`, `ListPolicyEngines`, `ListPolicyGenerationAssets`, or the policies' `GetPolicy` and `ListPolicies` can read that data in plaintext.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreatePolicyEngine` | `$.encryptionKeyArn` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:GetPolicyEngine` | *(any parameter)* |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:ListPolicyEngines` | *(any parameter)* |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:ListPolicyGenerationAssets` | `$.policyGenerationId` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.PolicyEngine.5

IAM principal, with unintended IAM permissions to read the description, policy definitions, and policy generation assets from an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore policy engine that has been encrypted with an AWS owned KMS key, can read the description, policy definitions, and policy generation assets in the policy engine.

**Impacts:** [Data Collection](../threat-impacts.md#data-collection), [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.PolicyEngine.1](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlpolicyengine1)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1048](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1048/), [T1213](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1213/)

**Scoping** (for [Unauthorized data access through AWS owned KMS key](../potential-threats.md#unauthorized-data-access-through-aws-owned-kms-key)): By default, your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore policy engine's description, policy definitions, and policy generation assets are encrypted at rest with an AWS owned key. That key type gives you no key policy to govern, no audit record of key use, and no control over the key lifecycle, so an IAM principal granted broader permissions than intended can retrieve them in plaintext.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:GetPolicyEngine` | *(any parameter)* |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:ListPolicyGenerationAssets` | `$.policyGenerationId` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Registry.1

Threat actor, with knowledge of a flawed inbound registry custom JWT authorizer configuration, can take advantage of the flawed inbound registry custom JWT authorizer configuration to gain unauthorized access to the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore registry.

**Impacts:** [Account and Resource Discovery](../threat-impacts.md#account-and-resource-discovery), [Initial Access](../threat-impacts.md#initial-access)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Registry.1](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlregistry1), [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Registry.3](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlregistry3)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1078.004](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/004/), [T1526](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1526/)

**Scoping** (for [Flawed authentication model problem](../potential-threats.md#flawed-authentication-model-problem)): The inbound custom JWT authorizer configuration of your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore registry admits callers to its search API and MCP endpoint when their bearer tokens pass its issuer and claim rules. A defect in those issuer and claim rules can let a threat actor gain unauthorized access to the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore registry.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore:SearchRegistryRecords` | `$.registryIds[*]`, `$.searchQuery` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Registry.2

IAM principal, with IAM permissions to create an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore registry's identity provider private endpoint, can create the identity provider private endpoint in a single Availability Zone.

**Impacts:** [Endpoint Denial of Service](../threat-impacts.md#endpoint-denial-of-service)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Registry.2](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlregistry2)

**Scoping** (for [Service disruption from single availability zone dependency](../potential-threats.md#service-disruption-from-single-availability-zone-dependency)): An IAM principal with permissions to create an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore registry's identity provider private endpoint can use the subnets in `$.authorizerConfiguration.customJWTAuthorizer.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.subnetIds[*]` to place the network interfaces of the endpoint's VPC Lattice resource gateway in a single Availability Zone. An impairment of that zone can then leave the registry's JWT authorizer unable to reach your identity provider and interrupt `SearchRegistryRecords` calls and MCP endpoint requests from registry consumers.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateRegistry` | `$.authorizerConfiguration.customJWTAuthorizer.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.subnetIds[*]` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateRegistry` | `$.authorizerConfiguration.optionalValue.customJWTAuthorizer.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.subnetIds[*]` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Registry.3

Threat actor, with knowledge of a vulnerable OIDC identity provider that has been configured in the custom JWT authorizer of an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore registry, can gain federated access to the registry's search API and MCP endpoint and the approved records they return.

**Impacts:** [Initial Access](../threat-impacts.md#initial-access)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Registry.1](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlregistry1), [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Registry.3](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlregistry3)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1190](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/)

**Scoping** (for [Vulnerable identity provider problem](../potential-threats.md#vulnerable-identity-provider-problem)): An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore registry delegates authentication for its search API and MCP endpoint to the external OpenID Connect identity provider you choose for JWT-based authorization. If that identity provider is vulnerable, a threat actor presenting a signed JWT from that provider can gain federated access to approved records in your registry.

**Request parameters**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore:SearchRegistryRecords` | `$.registryIds[*]`, `$.searchQuery` |

### Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Registry.4

Threat actor, with control of an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore registry configured with overly permissive outbound security group rules, can use the registry to interact with ungoverned network destinations.

**Impacts:** [Data Exfiltration](../threat-impacts.md#data-exfiltration), [Defense Evasion](../threat-impacts.md#defense-evasion)

**Mitigations:** [Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Registry.4](#mitigationbedrock-agentcore-controlregistry4)

**Frameworks:** MITRE ATT&CK [T1048](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1048/)

**Protocols:** `HTTPS`

**Scoping** (for [Data exfiltration through overly-permissive outbound security group rules](../potential-threats.md#data-exfiltration-through-overly-permissive-outbound-security-group-rules)): The outbound rules of the security groups you specify for your registry's private endpoint, or of your VPC's default security group, govern connections from the endpoint's network interfaces in your subnets to destinations set in the registry's configuration. Where those rules permit an unrestricted destination range, a threat actor controlling the registry can use it to interact with ungoverned network destinations.

Untrusted IAM principal, that has been granted access to my Amazon Bedrock AgentCore registry record's IAM sync role through its trust policy, can assume my sync role and act with its permissions.

## Mitigations

Each scoping statement below names the capability the mitigation goal governs on the entity and the objective of governing it. Each mitigation's implementations describe how to govern or monitor that capability.

### Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.1

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Control service API calls on a governed VPC network should only be made against trusted resources or AWS service-owned resources

**Goal:** [Resource Perimeter - Only trusted resources can be accessed from my network](../mitigation-goals.md#resource-perimeter---only-trusted-resources-can-be-accessed-from-my-network)

**Addresses:** [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.2](#threatbedrock-agentcore-control2)

**Implemented by:** [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.1](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-control1), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.2](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-control2)

**Scoping** (for [Resource Perimeter - Only trusted resources can be accessed from my network](../mitigation-goals.md#resource-perimeter---only-trusted-resources-can-be-accessed-from-my-network)): Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Control API calls from your VPCs can target AgentCore resources in another account. Restricting those calls to resources in your organization enforces the resource perimeter on your network.

**Configure via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `ec2:CreateVpcEndpoint` | `$.PolicyDocument` |
| `ec2:ModifyVpcEndpoint` | `$.PolicyDocument` |

**Verify via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `ec2:DescribeVpcEndpoints` | `$.VpcEndpointId` |

### Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.2

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Control service API calls on a governed VPC network should only be made by trusted identities or AWS services

**Goal:** [Identity Perimeter - Only trusted identities are allowed from my network](../mitigation-goals.md#identity-perimeter---only-trusted-identities-are-allowed-from-my-network)

**Addresses:** [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.1](#threatbedrock-agentcore-control1)

**Implemented by:** [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.3](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-control3), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.4](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-control4)

**Scoping** (for [Identity Perimeter - Only trusted identities are allowed from my network](../mitigation-goals.md#identity-perimeter---only-trusted-identities-are-allowed-from-my-network)): Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Control API calls from your VPCs can be made by identities outside your organization. Restricting those calls to principals in your organization enforces the identity perimeter on your network.

**Configure via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `ec2:CreateVpcEndpoint` | `$.PolicyDocument` |
| `ec2:ModifyVpcEndpoint` | `$.PolicyDocument` |

**Verify via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `ec2:DescribeVpcEndpoints` | `$.VpcEndpointId` |

### Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.1

An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime's execution role should be restricted to accessing resources only from expected networks

**Goal:** [Network Perimeter - My identities can access resources only from expected networks](../mitigation-goals.md#network-perimeter---my-identities-can-access-resources-only-from-expected-networks)

**Addresses:** [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.12](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime12)

**Implemented by:** [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.1](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime1), [ManagedControl.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.1](#managedcontrolbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime1)

**Scoping** (for [Network Perimeter - My identities can access resources only from expected networks](../mitigation-goals.md#network-perimeter---my-identities-can-access-resources-only-from-expected-networks)): The `$.roleArn` request parameter designates your agent runtime's IAM execution role, and your agent or tool code calls AWS services with that role's credentials. Restricting those calls to expected networks enforces the network perimeter on your identities and helps prevent the use of those credentials from unexpected networks.

**Configure via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateAgentRuntime` | `$.networkConfiguration.networkMode`, `$.networkConfiguration.networkModeConfig.subnets[*]`, `$.roleArn` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateAgentRuntime` | `$.networkConfiguration.networkMode`, `$.networkConfiguration.networkModeConfig.subnets[*]`, `$.roleArn` |

**Verify via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:GetAgentRuntime` | `$.agentRuntimeId`, `$.agentRuntimeVersion` |

### Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.2

An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime's execution role should be assumed only by AgentCore acting on behalf of trusted resources

**Goal:** [Restrict IAM Role Assumption - Service or Execution Role](../mitigation-goals.md#restrict-iam-role-assumption---service-or-execution-role)

**Addresses:** [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.11](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime11)

**Implemented by:** [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.2](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime2), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.3](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime3), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.4](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime4), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.5](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime5)

**Scoping** (for [Restrict IAM Role Assumption - Service or Execution Role](../mitigation-goals.md#restrict-iam-role-assumption---service-or-execution-role)): Your agent runtime binds its IAM execution role through the `$.roleArn` request parameter, and the role's trust policy specifies which principals can assume it. Allowing only AgentCore, acting on behalf of trusted resources, to assume the role helps prevent an unintended principal from assuming it.

**Configure via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateAgentRuntime` | `$.roleArn` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateAgentRuntime` | `$.roleArn` |

**Verify via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:GetAgentRuntime` | `$.agentRuntimeId`, `$.agentRuntimeVersion` |

### Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.3

An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime should be accessed only from expected networks

**Goal:** [Network Perimeter - My resources can only be accessed from expected networks](../mitigation-goals.md#network-perimeter---my-resources-can-only-be-accessed-from-expected-networks)

**Addresses:** [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.8](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime8)

**Implemented by:** [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.6](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime6), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.7](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime7)

**Scoping** (for [Network Perimeter - My resources can only be accessed from expected networks](../mitigation-goals.md#network-perimeter---my-resources-can-only-be-accessed-from-expected-networks)): Amazon Bedrock AgentCore API calls to your agent runtime can originate from the internet and from your VPCs through an interface VPC endpoint (powered by AWS PrivateLink), and your agent runtime's resource-based policy specifies which principals can invoke it. A network perimeter helps you confirm that your agent runtime can be accessed only from expected networks.

**Configure via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:PutResourcePolicy` | `$.policy` |

**Verify via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:GetResourcePolicy` | `$.resourceArn` |

### Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.4

IAM principals should be restricted to accessing only trusted Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime resources

**Goal:** [Resource Perimeter - My identities can access only trusted resources](../mitigation-goals.md#resource-perimeter---my-identities-can-access-only-trusted-resources)

**Addresses:** [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.6](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime6)

**Implemented by:** [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.8](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime8)

**Scoping** (for [Resource Perimeter - My identities can access only trusted resources](../mitigation-goals.md#resource-perimeter---my-identities-can-access-only-trusted-resources)): Resource-based policies on an agent runtime and its endpoint in another account can grant your principals access to invoke that runtime. The resource perimeter helps restrict your identities to resources your organization owns.

**Configure via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `organizations:AttachPolicy` | `$.PolicyId`, `$.TargetId` |
| `organizations:CreatePolicy` | `$.Content`, `$.Type` |
| `organizations:UpdatePolicy` | `$.Content`, `$.PolicyId` |

**Verify via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `organizations:DescribePolicy` | `$.PolicyId` |
| `organizations:ListPolicies` | `$.Filter` |
| `organizations:ListPoliciesForTarget` | `$.Filter`, `$.TargetId` |
| `organizations:ListTargetsForPolicy` | `$.PolicyId` |

### Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.5

An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime should be in an Amazon VPC

**Goal:** [VPC Deployment](../mitigation-goals.md#vpc-deployment)

**Addresses:** [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.2](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime2)

**Implemented by:** [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.9](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime9), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.10](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime10), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.11](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime11), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.12](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime12), [ManagedControl.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.1](#managedcontrolbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime1)

**Scoping** (for [VPC Deployment](../mitigation-goals.md#vpc-deployment)): VPC network mode places elastic network interfaces for your agent runtime in the VPC subnets you specify, governed by the security groups you choose. Placing an agent runtime in a VPC is optional and enables network-level isolation and access controls.

**Configure via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateAgentRuntime` | `$.networkConfiguration.networkMode`, `$.networkConfiguration.networkModeConfig.subnets[*]` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateAgentRuntime` | `$.networkConfiguration.networkMode`, `$.networkConfiguration.networkModeConfig.subnets[*]` |

**Verify via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:GetAgentRuntime` | `$.agentRuntimeId`, `$.agentRuntimeVersion` |

### Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.6

An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime should have elastic network interfaces (ENIs) in more than one Availability Zone (AZ)

**Goal:** [Multi-AZ ENI Deployment](../mitigation-goals.md#multi-az-eni-deployment)

**Addresses:** [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.7](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime7)

**Implemented by:** [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.13](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime13), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.14](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime14), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.15](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime15)

**Scoping** (for [Multi-AZ ENI Deployment](../mitigation-goals.md#multi-az-eni-deployment)): On the default microVM compute type, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore creates elastic network interfaces for your agent runtime's VPC configuration in the `$.networkConfiguration.networkModeConfig.subnets[*]` subnets. Placing those network interfaces in more than one Availability Zone provides network-level redundancy and helps keep connectivity available when one zone is disrupted.

**Configure via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateAgentRuntime` | `$.networkConfiguration.networkModeConfig.subnets[*]` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateAgentRuntime` | `$.networkConfiguration.networkModeConfig.subnets[*]` |

**Verify via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:GetAgentRuntime` | `$.agentRuntimeId`, `$.agentRuntimeVersion` |

### Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.7

An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime's resource policy should limit permissions to a subset of IAM principals, rather than granting access to all IAM principals

**Goal:** [Resource Policy - Enforce Explicit Principal Definition](../mitigation-goals.md#resource-policy---enforce-explicit-principal-definition)

**Addresses:** [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.5](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime5)

**Implemented by:** [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.7](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime7), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.16](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime16), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.17](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime17)

**Scoping** (for [Resource Policy - Enforce Explicit Principal Definition](../mitigation-goals.md#resource-policy---enforce-explicit-principal-definition)): An agent runtime can carry its own resource-based policy that names the IAM principals allowed to perform invocation and session actions, set through `$.policy`. Requiring explicit principal definitions rather than wildcard principals helps prevent the agent runtime from inadvertently being made public or accessible to unintended actors. This mitigation applies to an agent runtime whose callers authenticate as IAM principals (SigV4). An agent runtime configured with OAuth (JWT) inbound authorization must name a wildcard principal instead, so this mitigation does not apply to it.

**Configure via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:PutResourcePolicy` | `$.policy` |

**Verify via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:GetResourcePolicy` | `$.resourceArn` |

### Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.8

An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime should only be configured with a trusted OpenID Connect identity provider

**Goal:** [Resource Configuration - Trusted Targets](../mitigation-goals.md#resource-configuration---trusted-targets)

**Addresses:** [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.1](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime1)

**Implemented by:** [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.18](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime18), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.19](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime19), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.20](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime20)

**Scoping** (for [Resource Configuration - Trusted Targets](../mitigation-goals.md#resource-configuration---trusted-targets)): An agent runtime sets its inbound JWT authorizer through `$.authorizerConfiguration.customJWTAuthorizer.discoveryUrl`, which can name OpenID Connect identity providers outside AWS. Restricting the inbound JWT authorizer helps keep the bearer tokens your agent runtime accepts flowing only from trusted targets.

**Configure via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateAgentRuntime` | `$.authorizerConfiguration.customJWTAuthorizer.discoveryUrl` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateAgentRuntime` | `$.authorizerConfiguration.customJWTAuthorizer.discoveryUrl` |

**Verify via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:GetAgentRuntime` | `$.agentRuntimeId`, `$.agentRuntimeVersion` |

### Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.9

An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime should be accessed only by trusted identities or AWS services acting on behalf of trusted resources

**Goal:** [Identity Perimeter - Only trusted identities can access my resources](../mitigation-goals.md#identity-perimeter---only-trusted-identities-can-access-my-resources)

**Addresses:** [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.9](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime9)

**Implemented by:** [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.21](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime21), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.22](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime22), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.23](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime23)

**Scoping** (for [Identity Perimeter - Only trusted identities can access my resources](../mitigation-goals.md#identity-perimeter---only-trusted-identities-can-access-my-resources)): An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime supports a resource-based policy that specifies who can access it and what actions they can perform. The identity perimeter helps restrict access to your agent runtimes to trusted identities and AWS services acting on your behalf.

**Configure via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:PutResourcePolicy` | `$.policy` |

**Verify via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:GetResourcePolicy` | `$.resourceArn` |

### Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.10

An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime that uses an inbound JWT authorizer to authenticate principals should be configured only with trusted OIDC or OAuth 2.0 authorization server providers

**Goal:** [Trusted SSO Configuration](../mitigation-goals.md#trusted-sso-configuration)

**Addresses:** [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.4](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime4), [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.10](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime10)

**Implemented by:** [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.24](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime24), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.25](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime25)

**Scoping** (for [Trusted SSO Configuration](../mitigation-goals.md#trusted-sso-configuration)): An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime can authenticate callers that invoke it with JWT bearer tokens from the OpenID Connect (OIDC) or OAuth 2.0 authorization server provider designated by `$.authorizerConfiguration.customJWTAuthorizer.discoveryUrl`, the provider's discovery URL. Configuring only trusted OIDC or OAuth 2.0 authorization server providers helps prevent an untrusted identity provider from being used to gain unintended access.

**Configure via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateAgentRuntime` | `$.authorizerConfiguration.customJWTAuthorizer.allowedAudience[*]`, `$.authorizerConfiguration.customJWTAuthorizer.allowedClients[*]`, `$.authorizerConfiguration.customJWTAuthorizer.discoveryUrl` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateAgentRuntime` | `$.authorizerConfiguration.customJWTAuthorizer.allowedAudience[*]`, `$.authorizerConfiguration.customJWTAuthorizer.allowedClients[*]`, `$.authorizerConfiguration.customJWTAuthorizer.discoveryUrl` |

**Verify via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:GetAgentRuntime` | `$.agentRuntimeId`, `$.agentRuntimeVersion` |

### Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.11

An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime should be tagged with information that describes the owner and purpose

**Goal:** [Resource Tagging - Owner and Purpose](../mitigation-goals.md#resource-tagging---owner-and-purpose)

**Addresses:** [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.3](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime3)

**Implemented by:** [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.26](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime26), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.27](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime27), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.28](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime28)

**Scoping** (for [Resource Tagging - Owner and Purpose](../mitigation-goals.md#resource-tagging---owner-and-purpose)): You can tag an agent runtime by calling `CreateAgentRuntime`, whose `$.tags{key}` request parameter carries a key-to-value map, or later by calling `TagResource`. Owner and purpose tags help track ownership and the business function each agent runtime supports.

**Configure via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateAgentRuntime` | `$.tags{key}` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:TagResource` | `$.tags{key}` |

**Verify via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:ListTagsForResource` | `$.resourceArn` |

### Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.12

An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime should be associated only with security groups whose inbound and outbound rules restrict traffic to only the required sources, destinations, protocols, and ports

**Goal:** [Restrict Security Group Access](../mitigation-goals.md#restrict-security-group-access)

**Addresses:** [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.15](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime15)

**Implemented by:** [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.29](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime29), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.30](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime30), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.31](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime31)

**Scoping** (for [Restrict Security Group Access](../mitigation-goals.md#restrict-security-group-access)): AgentCore attaches the security groups in `$.networkConfiguration.networkModeConfig.securityGroups[*]` to the elastic network interfaces it creates in your subnets in VPC network mode, and the groups in `$.authorizerConfiguration.customJWTAuthorizer.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.securityGroupIds[*]` can replace your VPC's default security group on the managed VPC Lattice resource gateway that your inbound JWT authorizer uses to reach a private identity provider. Restricting the inbound and outbound rules to the required sources, destinations, protocols, and ports helps reduce the network exposure of your agent runtime.

**Configure via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateAgentRuntime` | `$.authorizerConfiguration.customJWTAuthorizer.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.securityGroupIds[*]`, `$.networkConfiguration.networkModeConfig.securityGroups[*]` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateAgentRuntime` | `$.authorizerConfiguration.customJWTAuthorizer.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.securityGroupIds[*]`, `$.networkConfiguration.networkModeConfig.securityGroups[*]` |

**Verify via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:GetAgentRuntime` | `$.agentRuntimeId`, `$.agentRuntimeVersion` |

### Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.13

An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime should be configured to send application and trace logs to CloudWatch Logs using vended logs delivery

**Goal:** [CloudWatch Logging - Vended Logs Delivery V2](../mitigation-goals.md#cloudwatch-logging---vended-logs-delivery-v2)

**Addresses:** [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.13](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime13), [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.14](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime14)

**Implemented by:** [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.32](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime32), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntime.33](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntime33)

**Scoping** (for [CloudWatch Logging - Vended Logs Delivery V2](../mitigation-goals.md#cloudwatch-logging---vended-logs-delivery-v2)): AgentCore Runtime produces application logs for each invocation of your agent runtime, recording the invocation's operation, request ID, session ID and request payload, and trace spans for each `InvokeAgentRuntime` call, recording the agent runtime, endpoint, session ID, latency and error type. Sending those logs to CloudWatch Logs using vended logs delivery provides security-relevant visibility.

**Configure via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `cloudwatch-logs:CreateDelivery` | `$.deliveryDestinationArn`, `$.deliverySourceName` |
| `cloudwatch-logs:PutDeliveryDestination` | `$.deliveryDestinationConfiguration.destinationResourceArn`, `$.deliveryDestinationType` |
| `cloudwatch-logs:PutDeliverySource` | `$.logType` |

**Verify via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `cloudwatch-logs:GetDelivery` | `$.id` |
| `cloudwatch-logs:GetDeliveryDestination` | `$.name` |
| `cloudwatch-logs:GetDeliverySource` | `$.name` |

### Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntimeEndpoint.3

An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent runtime endpoint's resource policy should limit permissions to a subset of IAM principals, rather than granting access to all IAM principals

**Goal:** [Resource Policy - Enforce Explicit Principal Definition](../mitigation-goals.md#resource-policy---enforce-explicit-principal-definition)

**Addresses:** [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntimeEndpoint.2](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntimeendpoint2)

**Implemented by:** [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntimeEndpoint.2](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntimeendpoint2), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntimeEndpoint.4](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntimeendpoint4), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.AgentRuntimeEndpoint.5](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlagentruntimeendpoint5)

**Scoping** (for [Resource Policy - Enforce Explicit Principal Definition](../mitigation-goals.md#resource-policy---enforce-explicit-principal-definition)): An agent runtime endpoint can carry its own resource-based policy that names the IAM principals allowed to invoke the endpoint, set through `$.policy`. Requiring explicit principal definitions rather than wildcard principals helps prevent the agent runtime endpoint from inadvertently being made public or accessible to unintended actors. This mitigation applies to an agent runtime endpoint whose callers authenticate as IAM principals (SigV4). An agent runtime endpoint configured with OAuth (JWT) inbound authorization must name a wildcard principal instead, so this mitigation does not apply to it.

**Configure via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:PutResourcePolicy` | `$.policy` |

**Verify via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:GetResourcePolicy` | `$.resourceArn` |

### Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Browser.1

### Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CapacityProvider.1

An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore capacity provider's default instance role, or instance profile where one is provided, should be restricted to accessing resources only from expected networks

**Goal:** [Network Perimeter - My identities can access resources only from expected networks](../mitigation-goals.md#network-perimeter---my-identities-can-access-resources-only-from-expected-networks)

**Addresses:** [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CapacityProvider.12](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlcapacityprovider12)

**Scoping** (for [Network Perimeter - My identities can access resources only from expected networks](../mitigation-goals.md#network-perimeter---my-identities-can-access-resources-only-from-expected-networks)): The default instance role that AgentCore creates for your capacity provider, or the instance profile where the `$.computeConfiguration.ec2Configuration.launchTemplateSource.launchParameters.instanceProfileArn` request parameter designates one, is the role attached to every Amazon EC2 managed instance your capacity provider launches, whose credentials host processes and SSH sessions on those instances read from instance metadata to call AWS services, while your agent code uses the agent runtime execution role rather than this role. **Configure via**

| Operation | Parameters |

| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateCapacityProvider` | `$.computeConfiguration.ec2Configuration.launchTemplateSource.launchParameters.instanceProfileArn` |

**Verify via**

|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:GetCapacityProvider` | `$.capacityProviderId` |

### Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.CapacityProvider.9

An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore capacity provider should have detailed monitoring enabled to collect detailed CloudWatch metrics

**Goal:** [Detailed CloudWatch Metrics](../mitigation-goals.md#detailed-cloudwatch-metrics)

**Scoping** (for [Detailed CloudWatch Metrics](../mitigation-goals.md#detailed-cloudwatch-metrics)): Detailed monitoring, turned on by setting the `$.computeConfiguration.ec2Configuration.launchTemplateSource.launchParameters.monitoring` request parameter to `DETAILED`, sends metrics for your capacity provider's Amazon EC2 managed instances to CloudWatch in 1-minute periods instead of the default 5-minute periods. Collecting those metrics improves security visibility by providing finer-grained data for anomaly detection and incident response.

**Reference:** If another monitoring platform already collects equivalent detailed metrics for this resource, that platform can provide the same visibility for anomaly detection and incident response. Enable this feature when no equivalent collection is in place.

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:GetCapacityProvider` | `$.capacityProviderId` |

**Scoping** (for [Restrict IAM Role Assumption - Service or Execution Role](../mitigation-goals.md#restrict-iam-role-assumption---service-or-execution-role)): Your gateway's IAM service role, passed in the `$.roleArn` request parameter, has a trust policy that specifies which principals can assume it. **Scoping** (for [Network Perimeter - My resources can only be accessed from expected networks](../mitigation-goals.md#network-perimeter---my-resources-can-only-be-accessed-from-expected-networks)): Requests to your gateway can originate from the internet through its public endpoint or from a VPC through an interface VPC endpoint (powered by AWS PrivateLink), and your gateway's resource-based policy can authorize them. A network perimeter helps you confirm that your gateway can be accessed only from expected networks.

### Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.3

IAM principals should be restricted to accessing only trusted Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway resources

### Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.4

An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway should be encrypted with an AWS KMS customer managed key

**Goal:** [KMS Customer Managed Key Encryption](../mitigation-goals.md#kms-customer-managed-key-encryption)

**Addresses:** [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.2](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlgateway2), [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.5](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlgateway5)

**Implemented by:** [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.8](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlgateway8), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.9](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlgateway9), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.10](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlgateway10)

**Scoping** (for [KMS Customer Managed Key Encryption](../mitigation-goals.md#kms-customer-managed-key-encryption)): When you call `CreateGateway` or `UpdateGateway`, the `$.kmsKeyArn` request parameter sets a customer managed AWS KMS key that encrypts your gateway's data at rest. Unlike the default AWS owned key, a customer managed key gives you control over its lifecycle and lets you audit its use. You can also make your gateway's encrypted data unavailable by disabling the key or revoking the gateway's access to it.

**Configure via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateGateway` | `$.kmsKeyArn` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateGateway` | `$.kmsKeyArn` |

**Verify via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:GetGateway` | `$.gatewayIdentifier` |

### Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.6

An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway's identity provider private endpoint should have elastic network interfaces (ENIs) in more than one Availability Zone (AZ)

**Goal:** [Multi-AZ ENI Deployment](../mitigation-goals.md#multi-az-eni-deployment)

**Scoping** (for [Multi-AZ ENI Deployment](../mitigation-goals.md#multi-az-eni-deployment)): For your gateway's identity provider private endpoint, AgentCore creates a managed VPC Lattice resource gateway with one network interface in each subnet of the `$.authorizerConfiguration.customJWTAuthorizer.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.subnetIds[*]` subnet list. Placing those network interfaces in more than one Availability Zone provides network-level redundancy and helps keep connectivity available when one zone is disrupted.

**Configure via**

| Operation | Parameters |

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:GetGateway` | `$.gatewayIdentifier` |

### Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.7

An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway's resource policy should limit permissions to a subset of IAM principals, rather than granting access to all IAM principals

**Goal:** [Resource Policy - Enforce Explicit Principal Definition](../mitigation-goals.md#resource-policy---enforce-explicit-principal-definition)

**Addresses:** [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.6](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlgateway6)

**Implemented by:** [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.6](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlgateway6), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.16](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlgateway16), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.17](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlgateway17)

**Scoping** (for [Resource Policy - Enforce Explicit Principal Definition](../mitigation-goals.md#resource-policy---enforce-explicit-principal-definition)): A gateway can carry its own resource-based policy that names the IAM principals allowed to invoke the gateway, set through `$.policy`. Requiring explicit principal definitions rather than wildcard principals helps prevent the gateway from inadvertently being made public or accessible to unintended actors. This mitigation applies to a gateway whose callers authenticate as IAM principals (SigV4). A gateway configured with OAuth (JWT) inbound authorization must name a wildcard principal instead, so this mitigation does not apply to it.

**Configure via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:PutResourcePolicy` | `$.policy` |

**Verify via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:GetResourcePolicy` | `$.resourceArn` |

Requiring authentication on that path helps prevent direct unauthenticated access to your gateway.

**Verify via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:GetGateway` | `$.gatewayIdentifier` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:ListGateways` | *(any parameter)* |

An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway should be configured to send application logs to CloudWatch Logs using vended logs delivery

**Goal:** [CloudWatch Logging - Vended Logs Delivery V2](../mitigation-goals.md#cloudwatch-logging---vended-logs-delivery-v2)

**Addresses:** [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.14](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlgateway14), [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.16](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlgateway16)

**Implemented by:** [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.36](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlgateway36), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Gateway.37](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlgateway37)

**Scoping** (for [CloudWatch Logging - Vended Logs Delivery V2](../mitigation-goals.md#cloudwatch-logging---vended-logs-delivery-v2)): As your gateway processes MCP requests, its application logs record authorization header errors, invalid tool or method parameters, target configuration errors, and request and response bodies. Sending those logs to CloudWatch Logs using vended logs delivery provides security-relevant visibility.

**Configure via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `cloudwatch-logs:CreateDelivery` | `$.deliveryDestinationArn`, `$.deliverySourceName` |
| `cloudwatch-logs:PutDeliveryDestination` | `$.deliveryDestinationConfiguration.destinationResourceArn`, `$.deliveryDestinationType` |
| `cloudwatch-logs:PutDeliverySource` | `$.logType` |

**Verify via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `cloudwatch-logs:GetDelivery` | `$.id` |
| `cloudwatch-logs:GetDeliveryDestination` | `$.name` |
| `cloudwatch-logs:GetDeliverySource` | `$.name` |

### Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.GatewayTarget.1

An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway target's private endpoint should be placed only in private subnets

**Goal:** [Private Subnet Placement](../mitigation-goals.md#private-subnet-placement)

**Addresses:** [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.GatewayTarget.4](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlgatewaytarget4)

**Implemented by:** [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.GatewayTarget.1](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlgatewaytarget1), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.GatewayTarget.2](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlgatewaytarget2)

**Scoping** (for [Private Subnet Placement](../mitigation-goals.md#private-subnet-placement)): For a managed private endpoint, the required `$.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.subnetIds[*]` request parameter sets the subnets that hold its VPC Lattice resource gateway network interfaces. Private subnet placement helps prevent direct internet routing to your gateway target's private endpoint, reducing its network exposure.

**Configure via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateGatewayTarget` | `$.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.endpointIpAddressType`, `$.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.subnetIds[*]` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateGatewayTarget` | `$.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.endpointIpAddressType`, `$.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.subnetIds[*]` |

**Verify via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:GetGatewayTarget` | `$.gatewayIdentifier`, `$.targetId` |

### Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.GatewayTarget.2

An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway target should be in an Amazon VPC

**Goal:** [VPC Deployment](../mitigation-goals.md#vpc-deployment)

**Addresses:** [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.GatewayTarget.2](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlgatewaytarget2)

**Implemented by:** [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.GatewayTarget.3](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlgatewaytarget3), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.GatewayTarget.4](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlgatewaytarget4), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.GatewayTarget.5](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlgatewaytarget5)

**Scoping** (for [VPC Deployment](../mitigation-goals.md#vpc-deployment)): With a private endpoint, a gateway target reaches its backend through a VPC Lattice resource gateway whose network interfaces sit in your VPC subnets. Placing a gateway target in a VPC is optional and enables network-level isolation and access controls.

**Configure via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateGatewayTarget` | `$.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.vpcIdentifier`, `$.privateEndpoint.selfManagedLatticeResource.resourceConfigurationIdentifier` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateGatewayTarget` | `$.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.vpcIdentifier`, `$.privateEndpoint.selfManagedLatticeResource.resourceConfigurationIdentifier` |

**Verify via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:GetGatewayTarget` | `$.gatewayIdentifier`, `$.targetId` |

### Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.GatewayTarget.3

An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway target's private endpoint should have elastic network interfaces (ENIs) in more than one Availability Zone (AZ)

**Goal:** [Multi-AZ ENI Deployment](../mitigation-goals.md#multi-az-eni-deployment)

**Addresses:** [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.GatewayTarget.3](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlgatewaytarget3)

**Implemented by:** [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.GatewayTarget.6](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlgatewaytarget6), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.GatewayTarget.7](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlgatewaytarget7), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.GatewayTarget.8](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlgatewaytarget8)

**Scoping** (for [Multi-AZ ENI Deployment](../mitigation-goals.md#multi-az-eni-deployment)): Amazon Bedrock AgentCore places the network interfaces of your gateway target's managed private endpoint in each subnet of the `$.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.subnetIds[*]` subnet list. Placing those network interfaces in more than one Availability Zone provides network-level redundancy and helps keep connectivity available when one zone is disrupted.

**Configure via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateGatewayTarget` | `$.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.subnetIds[*]` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateGatewayTarget` | `$.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.subnetIds[*]` |

**Verify via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:GetGatewayTarget` | `$.gatewayIdentifier`, `$.targetId` |

### Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.GatewayTarget.4

An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway target should only be configured with a trusted HTTP endpoint

**Goal:** [Resource Configuration - Trusted Targets](../mitigation-goals.md#resource-configuration---trusted-targets)

**Addresses:** [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.GatewayTarget.1](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlgatewaytarget1)

**Implemented by:** [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.GatewayTarget.9](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlgatewaytarget9), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.GatewayTarget.10](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlgatewaytarget10), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.GatewayTarget.11](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlgatewaytarget11)

**Scoping** (for [Resource Configuration - Trusted Targets](../mitigation-goals.md#resource-configuration---trusted-targets)): An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway target sets its endpoint through `$.targetConfiguration.mcp.mcpServer.endpoint`, `$.targetConfiguration.http.passthrough.endpoint`, `$.targetConfiguration.inference.provider.endpoint` or the Smithy model's endpoint rule set from `$.targetConfiguration.mcp.smithyModel.inlinePayload` or `$.targetConfiguration.mcp.smithyModel.s3.uri`, which can name HTTP endpoints outside AWS. Restricting the endpoint helps keep tool calls, model requests and outbound credentials flowing only to trusted targets.

**Configure via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateGatewayTarget` | `$.targetConfiguration.http.passthrough.endpoint`, `$.targetConfiguration.inference.provider.endpoint`, `$.targetConfiguration.mcp.mcpServer.endpoint`, `$.targetConfiguration.mcp.openApiSchema.inlinePayload`, `$.targetConfiguration.mcp.openApiSchema.s3.uri`, `$.targetConfiguration.mcp.smithyModel.inlinePayload`, `$.targetConfiguration.mcp.smithyModel.s3.uri` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateGatewayTarget` | `$.targetConfiguration.http.passthrough.endpoint`, `$.targetConfiguration.inference.provider.endpoint`, `$.targetConfiguration.mcp.mcpServer.endpoint`, `$.targetConfiguration.mcp.openApiSchema.inlinePayload`, `$.targetConfiguration.mcp.openApiSchema.s3.uri`, `$.targetConfiguration.mcp.smithyModel.inlinePayload`, `$.targetConfiguration.mcp.smithyModel.s3.uri` |

**Verify via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:GetGatewayTarget` | `$.gatewayIdentifier`, `$.targetId` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:ListGatewayTargets` | `$.gatewayIdentifier` |

### Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.GatewayTarget.5

An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gateway target's managed VPC Lattice resource gateway should be associated only with security groups whose inbound and outbound rules restrict traffic to only the required sources, destinations, protocols, and ports

**Goal:** [Restrict Security Group Access](../mitigation-goals.md#restrict-security-group-access)

**Addresses:** [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.GatewayTarget.5](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlgatewaytarget5)

**Implemented by:** [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.GatewayTarget.12](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlgatewaytarget12), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.GatewayTarget.13](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlgatewaytarget13), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.GatewayTarget.14](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlgatewaytarget14)

**Scoping** (for [Restrict Security Group Access](../mitigation-goals.md#restrict-security-group-access)): For a managed private endpoint, you can associate your own security groups with the managed VPC Lattice resource gateway's network interfaces through `$.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.securityGroupIds[*]` instead of the VPC's default security group. Restricting the inbound and outbound rules to the required sources, destinations, protocols, and ports helps reduce the network exposure of the managed VPC Lattice resource gateway.

**Configure via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateGatewayTarget` | `$.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.securityGroupIds[*]` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateGatewayTarget` | `$.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.securityGroupIds[*]` |

**Verify via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:GetGatewayTarget` | `$.gatewayIdentifier`, `$.targetId` |

### Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Harness.1

An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness's execution role should be restricted to accessing resources only from expected networks

**Goal:** [Network Perimeter - My identities can access resources only from expected networks](../mitigation-goals.md#network-perimeter---my-identities-can-access-resources-only-from-expected-networks)

**Addresses:** [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Harness.9](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlharness9)

**Implemented by:** [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Harness.1](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlharness1)

**Scoping** (for [Network Perimeter - My identities can access resources only from expected networks](../mitigation-goals.md#network-perimeter---my-identities-can-access-resources-only-from-expected-networks)): The `$.executionRoleArn` request parameter designates your harness's IAM execution role, and code in each session's microVM calls AWS services with that role's credentials. Restricting those calls to expected networks enforces the network perimeter on your identities and helps prevent the use of those credentials from unexpected networks.

**Configure via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateHarness` | `$.environment.agentCoreRuntimeEnvironment.networkConfiguration.networkMode`, `$.environment.agentCoreRuntimeEnvironment.networkConfiguration.networkModeConfig.subnets[*]`, `$.executionRoleArn` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateHarness` | `$.environment.agentCoreRuntimeEnvironment.networkConfiguration.networkMode`, `$.environment.agentCoreRuntimeEnvironment.networkConfiguration.networkModeConfig.subnets[*]`, `$.executionRoleArn` |

**Verify via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:GetHarness` | `$.harnessId`, `$.harnessVersion` |

### Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Harness.2

An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness's execution role should be assumed only by Amazon Bedrock AgentCore acting on behalf of trusted resources

**Goal:** [Restrict IAM Role Assumption - Service or Execution Role](../mitigation-goals.md#restrict-iam-role-assumption---service-or-execution-role)

**Addresses:** [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Harness.8](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlharness8)

**Scoping** (for [Restrict IAM Role Assumption - Service or Execution Role](../mitigation-goals.md#restrict-iam-role-assumption---service-or-execution-role)): You set your harness's IAM execution role through the `$.executionRoleArn` request parameter, and the role's trust policy specifies which principals can assume it. Allowing only Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, acting on behalf of trusted resources, to assume the role helps prevent an unintended principal from assuming it.

**Configure via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateHarness` | `$.executionRoleArn` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateHarness` | `$.executionRoleArn` |

**Verify via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:GetHarness` | `$.harnessId`, `$.harnessVersion` |

### Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Harness.4

An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness's managed memory should be encrypted with an AWS KMS customer managed key

**Goal:** [KMS Customer Managed Key Encryption](../mitigation-goals.md#kms-customer-managed-key-encryption)

**Addresses:** [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Harness.2](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlharness2), [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Harness.5](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlharness5)

**Implemented by:** [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Harness.8](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlharness8), [ManagedControl.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Harness.2](#managedcontrolbedrock-agentcore-controlharness2)

**Scoping** (for [KMS Customer Managed Key Encryption](../mitigation-goals.md#kms-customer-managed-key-encryption)): Your harness's managed memory stores conversation events and long-term memory records, encrypted at rest with an AWS owned key by default. The `$.memory.managedMemoryConfiguration.encryptionKeyArn` request parameter of `CreateHarness` sets a customer managed key for that memory, and the memory's key can't be changed after creation. With a customer managed key, you control the key lifecycle and can audit its use or disable it to make the stored data unavailable.

**Configure via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateHarness` | `$.memory.managedMemoryConfiguration.encryptionKeyArn` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:UpdateHarness` | `$.memory.optionalValue.managedMemoryConfiguration.encryptionKeyArn` |

**Verify via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:GetHarness` | `$.harnessId` |

An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness that uses an inbound JWT authorizer to authenticate principals should be configured only with trusted OAuth 2.0 authorization servers or OIDC identity providers

**Goal:** [Trusted SSO Configuration](../mitigation-goals.md#trusted-sso-configuration)

**Addresses:** [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Harness.4](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlharness4), [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Harness.7](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlharness7)

**Implemented by:** [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Memory.5](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlmemory5)

**Scoping** (for [Resource Perimeter - My identities can access only trusted resources](../mitigation-goals.md#resource-perimeter---my-identities-can-access-only-trusted-resources)): A resource-based policy on an AgentCore Memory resource in another account can grant your principals access to its events and memory records. The resource perimeter helps restrict your identities to resources your organization owns.

**Configure via**

| `organizations:ListTargetsForPolicy` | `$.PolicyId` |

### Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Memory.3

An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore memory should be encrypted with an AWS KMS customer managed key

**Goal:** [KMS Customer Managed Key Encryption](../mitigation-goals.md#kms-customer-managed-key-encryption)

**Addresses:** [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Memory.1](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlmemory1), [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Memory.3](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlmemory3)

**Implemented by:** [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Memory.6](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlmemory6), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Memory.7](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlmemory7), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Memory.8](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controlmemory8), [ManagedControl.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Memory.1](#managedcontrolbedrock-agentcore-controlmemory1)

**Scoping** (for [KMS Customer Managed Key Encryption](../mitigation-goals.md#kms-customer-managed-key-encryption)): Amazon Bedrock AgentCore encrypts your memory's short-term events and long-term memory records at rest, by default with an AWS owned key. The `$.encryptionKeyArn` request parameter, available only when you create the memory, sets a customer managed AWS KMS key instead. With a customer managed key, you can control its lifecycle, audit its use, and disable it to make the stored data unavailable.

**Configure via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:CreateMemory` | `$.encryptionKeyArn` |

**Verify via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:GetMemory` | `$.memoryId` |

### Mitigation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Memory.5

An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore memory should be configured to send APPLICATION_LOGS and TRACES logs to CloudWatch Logs using vended logs delivery

**Goal:** [CloudWatch Logging - Vended Logs Delivery V2](../mitigation-goals.md#cloudwatch-logging---vended-logs-delivery-v2)

**Scoping** (for [CloudWatch Logging - Vended Logs Delivery V2](../mitigation-goals.md#cloudwatch-logging---vended-logs-delivery-v2)): For your memory, AgentCore produces APPLICATION_LOGS that record `DeleteMemory` operations and long-term memory extraction and consolidation, and TRACES spans that record `CreateEvent`, `GetEvent`, `ListEvents`, `DeleteEvent`, `RetrieveMemoryRecords` and `ListMemoryRecords` calls, each with memory, session, event, actor or namespace identifiers. | `cloudwatch-logs:GetDelivery` | `$.id` |

| `cloudwatch-logs:GetDeliverySource` | `$.name` |

**Scoping** (for [Multi-AZ ENI Deployment](../mitigation-goals.md#multi-az-eni-deployment)): For your managed private endpoint, AgentCore Identity creates an Amazon VPC Lattice resource gateway whose network interfaces reside in the subnets listed in the `$.oauth2ProviderConfigInput.customOauth2ProviderConfig.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.subnetIds[*]` request parameter. **Addresses:** [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Oauth2CredentialProvider.2](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controloauth2credentialprovider2), [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Oauth2CredentialProvider.4](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controloauth2credentialprovider4)

**Scoping** (for [Trusted SSO Configuration](../mitigation-goals.md#trusted-sso-configuration)): An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore OAuth2 credential provider designates, through the vendor in `$.credentialProviderVendor` and its issuer and endpoint URLs, the OAuth 2.0 identity provider that authenticates your end users and issues your agents' tokens. **Verify via**

| Operation | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:GetOauth2CredentialProvider` | `$.name` |
| `bedrock-agentcore-control:ListOauth2CredentialProviders` | *(any parameter)* |

An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore OAuth2 credential provider's private endpoint should be associated only with security groups whose inbound and outbound rules restrict traffic to only the required sources, destinations, protocols, and ports

**Goal:** [Restrict Security Group Access](../mitigation-goals.md#restrict-security-group-access)

**Addresses:** [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Oauth2CredentialProvider.7](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controloauth2credentialprovider7)

**Implemented by:** [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Oauth2CredentialProvider.9](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controloauth2credentialprovider9), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Oauth2CredentialProvider.10](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controloauth2credentialprovider10), [Implementation.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.Oauth2CredentialProvider.11](#implementationbedrock-agentcore-controloauth2credentialprovider11)

**Scoping** (for [Restrict Security Group Access](../mitigation-goals.md#restrict-security-group-access)): When your OAuth2 credential provider uses a managed private endpoint, the security groups you can associate through `$.oauth2ProviderConfigInput.customOauth2ProviderConfig.privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.securityGroupIds[*]` or `$.oauth2ProviderConfigInput.customOauth2ProviderConfig.privateEndpointOverrides[*].privateEndpoint.managedVpcResource.securityGroupIds[*]` govern the traffic of the AgentCore-managed VPC Lattice resource gateway's network interfaces in your subnets, and the VPC's default security group is used if you specify none. **Addresses:** [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.PaymentManager.3](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlpaymentmanager3), [Threat.BEDROCK-AGENTCORE-CONTROL.PaymentManager.6](#threatbedrock-agentcore-controlpaymentmanager6)
